Re-extracting signal counts from the 14-year public point-source data with SkyLLH and profiling κ analytically, they find H_0=49⁺⁴⁰_-30 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ and β=0.67⁺⁰.16_-0.25, with the calorimetric β=1 disfavored at ∼2σ — the first population-level slope measurement, pointing to subcalorimetric coronae (Bethe-Heitler or synchrotron suppression).

Why it matters: this is a genuinely new distance rung immune to dust, absorption, scattering and radiative-transfer systematics — the entire error budget lives in source physics. As the digest frames it, it proposes a new rung rather than kicking away an old one. Caveats are candid and severe: the H_0 uncertainty is enormous and consistent with both Planck and SH0ES at 1σ; the value swings dramatically with the NGC 1068 intrinsic luminosity choice (H_0=109⁺²⁹_-37 if the high value is adopted) and with adding NGC 4151 as a second anchor (to H_0≈109, a ∼15% residual tension the authors attribute to intrinsic L_ν–L_X scatter). Selection on neutrino significance can also imprint a spurious correlation. IceCube-Gen2 could reach σ(H_0)≈16–20.

arXiv:2608.01289 — Combination of vector boson scattering measurements in leptonic final states at √(s)=13 TeV (CMS Collaboration)

CMS delivers its most comprehensive VBS combination: seven analyses over the full 138 fb⁻¹ Run 2 dataset, spanning same-sign and opposite-sign WW, WZ, ZZ, plus semileptonic WV/ZV channels, fit simultaneously across 48 phase-space regions and 1525 bins. A 4-POI model returns signal strengths all consistent with unity — μ_SSWW=1.05⁺⁰.15_-0.14, μ_OSWW=1.11±0.20 (6.4σ), μ_WZ=1.21⁺⁰.28_-0.25 (7.0σ), μ_ZZ=1.15⁺⁰.44_-0.37 (4.0σ) — with the combination sharpening OSWW and WZ uncertainties by up to 15% over the best individual inputs. A charge-separated 6-POI model probes the expected production charge asymmetry from the proton’s valence content, finding μ_W⁺W⁺⁼¹.13⁺⁰.17_-0.16 versus μ_W⁻W⁻⁼⁰.84⁺⁰.28_-0.24.

Why it matters: this is the consolidated stress-test of the electroweak-scattering program, coherently accounting for cross-channel correlations that single measurements cannot — the reference point against which unitarity-violating BSM effects in longitudinal boson scattering would appear as event excesses. Everything is SM-consistent, so it functions as a benchmark and a clean baseline for the EFT/anomalous-coupling recasts that follow. No tension is flagged; the correlations among signal strengths are mild.

arXiv:2608.00182 — Modification of Υ production in pO and OO collisions at LHCb (LHCb collaboration et al.)

Abstract only. LHCb measures Υ(2S) and Υ(3S) yields relative to Υ(1S) in pp, pO, and OO collisions. The pp ratios match earlier LHCb results; pO shows only slight relative suppression of the excited states, but OO suppresses the Υ(2S) by a factor of ∼2, with evidence for Υ(3S) suppression. The jump from a small pO effect to significant OO suppression is read as the onset of additional mechanisms — color screening in a deconfined medium — with QGP-formation models successfully describing the OO data.

Why it matters: alongside ALICE’s charm-sector v_2 splitting, this pushes the “how small can QGP be” question onto real Run 3 oxygen data, with sequential melting appearing in a system this small. The caveat, visible even from the abstract, is disentangling cold-nuclear-matter effects from genuine deconfinement screening — the pO reference is precisely what makes the OO excess interpretable, but the model dependence of the QGP interpretation remains.

item.title: Monday, August 3, 2026
item.description:
Dark sectors crowd the board

The day’s volume is dark matter — three separate dark-photon production stories, a monopole-DM construction, two new detection concepts, and an axion-WIMP dark-energy model — but the sharpest single result is a measurement: BESIII observes a charged charmoniumlike X(3790)⁻ near the D⁰D⁻ threshold at 5.3σ (arXiv:2607.29138), J^P=1⁻, extending the collaboration’s exotic-hadron run. Underneath, quantum-information language shows up twice as a genuine observable — in DIS and in top tomography — which is the one thread that carries forward from the recent tt̅ entanglement work.

Themes

Dark photon dark matter, three ways

A coincidental cluster attacking the same relic from different angles. Arora et al. arXiv:2607.29131 fit a freeze-in ALP + dark-photon pair to the Galactic 511 keV line; Kasamaki et al. arXiv:2607.29149 produce dark photons from inflationary quantum fluctuations in Starobinsky models, pinning m to 5.6–7.4 μeV once the frame-dependent kinetic function is tracked; and Cline et al. arXiv:2607.29682 revisit misaligned-dark-Higgs decay, mapping out 100 eV–1 GeV. Brümmer et al.’s 10⁸ GeV monopole DM arXiv:2607.29492 rounds out the dark-sector model-building, with ΔN_eff near current bounds as its handle.

Quantum information as a hadron and collider probe

Two papers use QI measures for real observables. Bloss et al. arXiv:2607.28724 argue entanglement, discord, steering and magic in DIS give complementary access to transverse-spin PDFs and the proton tensor charge — an EIC target. Erdogan et al. arXiv:2607.28761 use the full 15-parameter tt̅ two-qubit density matrix, now reconstructable, to constrain CP violation in the top Yukawa at one loop, competitive with tree-level tt̅H/tH. This is the collider-QI program from the citation radar moving from demonstration to measurement.

New ways to look for dark matter

Tsai et al. arXiv:2607.28722 propose Gravity Probe-DM: precision two-spacecraft ranging through the Sun’s downstream DM wake, with pre-fit response scales reaching nanometres over a year. Salces Pérez et al. arXiv:2607.28823 turn molecular-cloud ionization into a competitive bound on MeV DM and 10¹⁴–10¹⁷ g PBHs. On hardware, VORTEX arXiv:2607.28883 and TEXONO’s reactor ALP search arXiv:2607.29205 keep the haloscope/reactor programs ticking.

BESIII spectroscopy and flavor structure

Beyond the X(3790)⁻, Ghaderi et al. arXiv:2607.29223 fit the P_c/P_cs pentaquarks as meson-baryon molecules via Bethe-Salpeter, and Geng et al. arXiv:2607.29564 derive width-level CP sum rules from exact U-spin degeneracy. Stockdale et al. arXiv:2607.29331 classify the 25 minimal models generating b,c,τ masses radiatively — a different tack on flavor structure than last week’s CKM-texture wave.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.29138 — BESIII’s new charged charmoniumlike X(3790)⁻ at the D⁰D⁻ threshold, 5.3σ; the day’s cleanest observation.
  • arXiv:2607.28761 — First complete one-loop tt̅ density matrix turned into a CP-violation constraint on the top Yukawa via full quantum tomography.
  • arXiv:2607.28722 — Gravity Probe-DM: a purely gravitational, Solar-System map of local DM from spacecraft ranging through the Sun’s wake — ambitious and genuinely novel.
  • arXiv:2607.28724 — Entanglement, discord and magic in DIS as complementary probes of the proton tensor charge; QI meets hadron structure at the EIC.
  • arXiv:2607.29682 — Misaligned-dark-Higgs dark-photon DM, a predictive 100 eV–1 GeV window testable by CMB/Lyman-α and direct detection.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.29388 Halbach Magnetic Weber Bars — Domcke et al. (hep-ph) — strong-gradient magnet arrays for kHz–MHz GW searches, reaching S_h¹/2∼10⁻²¹/√(Hz).
  • arXiv:2607.29197 Testing the Hubble Tension in a Bianchi Type I Background — Tedesco (astro-ph.CO) — a worked shear→distance-quadrupole calculation concluding minimal anisotropy cannot resolve the tension; the anisotropic counterpart to the week’s tension walls.
  • arXiv:2607.28721 Natural Phantom Crossing from Axion-WIMP Interactions — Delaunay et al. (hep-ph) — a ℤ_N-protected route to DESI-like phantom crossing with percent-level growth suppression.
  • arXiv:2607.29352 pylhe: A Lightweight Python interface to Les Houches Event files — Neuwirth et al. (hep-ph) — columnar/Awkward-friendly LHE handling.
  • arXiv:2607.29508 The fundamental limit of jet tagging: Beyond top jets — Koller et al. (hep-ph) — the optimal-classifier gap is smaller for W/Z/H→gg than for tops.
  • arXiv:2607.29574 Generalized parton distributions from lattice QCD — Cichy et al. (hep-lat) — review of quasi- vs. pseudo-distribution GPD extractions.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.29138 — Observation of a Charged Charmoniumlike Structure in e⁺e⁻→D⁰D⁻π⁺⁺c.c. (BESIII Collaboration)

BESIII performs a partial-wave analysis of e⁺e⁻→D⁰D⁻π⁺ on 1667 pb⁻¹ collected at √(s)=4682 MeV, using combined single- and double-tag reconstruction. A near-threshold enhancement in the D⁰D⁻ system, modeled with a Flatté lineshape, requires J^P=1⁻ and yields mass (3794.7±6.0±8.7) MeV/c² and D⁰D⁻ coupling (1.6±0.2±0.2) GeV. The raw fit significance is 7.7σ; after 320 pseudo-experiments account for the look-elsewhere effect and systematics are folded in, it settles at 5.3σ — enough to claim observation of this new charged charmoniumlike state, X(3790)⁻. Cross-checks (alternative J^P<4, added PHSP or non-resonant amplitudes) leave the signal at ≥8σ when nuisance components are included. The analysis simultaneously updates the excited charmed mesons, with new D_2^(2460), D_1^(2600) and D_1^*(2760) parameters.

Why it matters: this is the first isovector state seen coupling to a (DD̅)^± pair — a channel previously argued unlikely, since spin-parity conservation forbids the DD̅π vertex under pure pion-exchange binding, yet phenomenology and lattice predict a scalar DD̅ bound state. A charged 1⁻ structure right at threshold extends the Z_c/X(3872) molecular narrative into a new final state and constrains heavy-quark-symmetry partner counting. Caveats: the fit fraction is small (1.3±0.3%), systematics on mass are large (±8.7 MeV), and the Flatté parameterization plus fixed D_3^(2750) and D̅^0-width inputs carry model dependence; the state’s nature (molecule vs. threshold cusp) is not resolved here.

arXiv:2607.28722 — Gravity Probe-DM: The Gravitational Laboratory for Dark Matter (Yu-Dai Tsai et al.)

Tsai and Foote propose a purely gravitational Solar-System dark-matter search exploiting the irreducible downstream wake the Sun’s gravity carves into any incident unbound DM flow. Two precision-ranged spacecraft act as a heliocentric gradiometer: a uniform acceleration cancels, but the wake tidal tensor projected along the baseline does not. For a LISA-like 2.5×10⁶ km baseline crossing a 0.1 AU coherent width at 30 km/s, a one-percent density excess gives a raw uniform-core range response of only 0.63 pm over the 5.77 d crossing. Because the free response grows as T² while the projected tide stays coherent, an axial “wake-skimming” arc lifts this to 2.5 nm over one year; an optimistic low-lag dark-disk benchmark (20% of local density, 30% focused contrast) reaches ~15 nm. REBOUND/REBOUNDx integrations validate the linear-in-density scaling and the ω̇∝M_od precession law.

Why it matters: existing planetary/asteroid-ephemeris bounds only limit smooth, near-spherical DM around the Sun; this concept instead targets an anisotropic, directional structure tied to the Galactic flow, giving a distinctive turn-on/turn-off tidal waveform and, for wave DM, de Broglie-scale interference. A detection would be the first Solar-System gravitational DM map and would calibrate the local phase-space model underlying direct detection. Caveats are substantial and stated plainly: nanometre signals sit beneath solar/planetary/asteroid tides, radiation pressure and thermal recoil; the T² enhancement requires a passive one-year dwell that is unavailable near 1 AU without going to several AU; and every number is a pre-fit response scale, not a demonstrated sensitivity. LISA Pathfinder archival data is proposed only as a methodological null test.

arXiv:2607.28761 — Quantum Tomography of Top Quarks as a Probe of Charge-Parity Violation (Eren Erdogan et al.)

Erdogan et al. compute the first fully renormalized one-loop Higgs-induced correction to the tt̅ production spin density matrix from a CP-mixed top-Yukawa coupling ℒ=-(m_t/v)h t̅(a_t+ib_tγ_5)t, predicting its imprint on all fifteen Fano coefficients. The couplings enter at 𝒪(y_t²/16π²⁾; CP-odd effects are linear in a_tb_t and populate specifically the antisymmetric correlation C_nr⁻ (dispersive) and the polarization difference P_k-P̅_k (absorptive), none of which shift the cross section. On-shell renormalization forces imaginary top field-renormalization constants ∝a_tb_t — the first complete renormalized CP-odd density matrix. Confronting CMS’s full 15-parameter tomography with its covariance, they find at a_t=1 the bound -1.40<b_t<1.23 (95% CL, inclusive Fano fit), tightening to -1.01<b_t<1.26 when spin and m_tt̅-shape information are combined — comparable to ATLAS’s |b_t|≈1.1 from tree-level tt̅H/tH.

Why it matters: this converts the collider quantum-information program from demonstrating entanglement/magic to a genuine precision measurement, using the reconstructed quantum state itself as the observable. The method is model-agnostic — any operator shifting the density matrix can be confronted with the same tomography without regenerating events. Caveats: the SM sits within 68% CL, so this is a constraint not a hint; the bound assumes all other new physics decouples from the loop; and the existing binning was optimized for quantum-property studies, so finer m_tt̅ bins near threshold — where Higgs corrections peak — would sharpen sensitivity. Two mirror minima under (a_t,b_t)→(-a_t,-b_t) remain unresolved.

item.title: Friday, July 31, 2026
item.description:
A collider slate and a flavor coincidence

The day’s bulk is an ATLAS document dump built around τ final states, anchored by a genuinely useful precision number from the other side of the ring: CMS measures m_H=125.13±0.15 GeV in diphoton arXiv:2607.28396, the most precise single-channel value to date. The most interesting theory paper is a flavor coincidence dressed up as a mechanism — Arkani-Hamed et al. arXiv:2607.27315 arguing the CKM unitarity-triangle angles sit at simple multiples of π/8 — which picks up directly from yesterday’s geometric-CKM speculation. And Bao et al. arXiv:2607.27313 answer yesterday’s GW-decay paper with a wall: nonclassical effects of weakly coupled waves are doubly suppressed.

Themes

ATLAS’s tau slate, plus a sharper Higgs mass

Alongside CMS’s diphoton mass arXiv:2607.28396, ATLAS posts a stack of τ-channel results: tt̅H/tH in H→ττ arXiv:2607.27276 and a tH combination arXiv:2607.27708 giving μ_tH=3.3⁺¹.7_-1.5 (the most precise tH yet), heavy Majorana neutrinos in same-sign-τ VBS arXiv:2607.27307, and a boosted di-τ resonance with tt̅ arXiv:2607.28484. Plus Z’→ℓℓ (Z’_SSM>5.5 TeV, arXiv:2607.28334) and a first VLQ→top+diphoton search arXiv:2607.28381. The dedicated boosted di-τ reconstruction recurs across these — the tool that debuted in the July 27 boosted H→ττ measurement is now standard equipment.

Flavor structure, top-down

Arkani-Hamed et al. arXiv:2607.27315 parametrize the Yukawas with sparse “nine-link textures” and find the fitted CP phases cluster at multiples of π/8, reproducing (α,β,γ)≈(π/2,π/8,3π/8) with calculable, near-term-testable deviations — and a bonus route to strong CP via naturally real determinants. It lands the day after Lin’s geometric CKM reparameterization arXiv:2607.26681; two swings at the same empirical pattern in as many days. Benavides et al.’s three-texture-zero seesaw fit arXiv:2607.28549 is the workmanlike counterpart.

Small-scale structure as a DM lab

A coherent cluster mines galactic scales for DM microphysics: the SatGen semi-analytic dwarf-density pair, Part I finding a ~2.4σ central-density diversity tension with CDM arXiv:2607.27316 and Part II recasting Fermi-LAT J-factor limits arXiv:2607.27326; particle-in-cell evolution of dark-plasma subhalos arXiv:2607.27312; Q-ball cusp-flattening arXiv:2607.28517; and Nadler et al.’s review arXiv:2607.28564.

Quantum limits on weakly-coupled waves

Bao et al. arXiv:2607.27313 prove two obstructions — coarse-grained detector modes and extra powers of the weak coupling — that suppress any nonclassical signature of axion-DM or GW fields, explicitly ruling out proposals to establish quantized gravity from GW observations. Read it against yesterday’s Blas–Oller GW→γγ decay claim arXiv:2607.24930: the enthusiasm and the cold water arrived one day apart.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.28396 — CMS’s m_H=125.13±0.15 GeV in diphoton; the new precision benchmark, refined calibration and all.
  • arXiv:2607.27315 — Arkani-Hamed et al.’s π/8 flavor textures: a striking coincidence turned into falsifiable predictions for the unitarity-triangle angles.
  • arXiv:2607.27313 — Why weakly coupled waves stay classical; a general no-go that closes off the “quantized gravity from GWs” program.
  • arXiv:2607.27346 — ANAIS-112’s first bound on transverse-plasmon solar axions, a resonant production channel that can dominate Primakoff by two orders of magnitude at 35–280 eV.
  • arXiv:2607.27708 — ATLAS’s tH combination, μ_tH=3.3⁺¹.7_-1.5; the most precise handle yet on this rare, top-Yukawa-sign-sensitive mode.

From the community

Ivanov’s GGI lecture notes on large-scale-structure EFT arXiv:2607.28314 — a from-scratch pedagogical treatment aimed at students, timely given the DESI-driven interest in full-shape clustering.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.28095 Comment on “First Limits on Axion Dark Matter from a DALI Prototype” — Garutti et al. (hep-ex) — an independent assessment finding no mode below 12 GHz that supports the claimed sensitivity; a pointed methods critique.
  • arXiv:2607.28477 Design and beam-test of the CRILIN crystal calorimeter — Ceravolo et al. (physics.ins-det) — sub-20 ps timing above 60 GeV for future lepton colliders.
  • arXiv:2607.28113 (Hyper)Nuclei production in isobar collisions at RHIC — STAR Collaboration (nucl-ex) — hypertriton production favors a non-Gaussian wavefunction with more short-distance d–Λ content.
  • arXiv:2607.28214 Domain walls through different cosmologies — Dankovsky et al. (astro-ph.CO) — near-peak GW spectra are largely EoS-independent; the month’s defect thread continues.
  • arXiv:2607.27822 CLVisc Agent — Wang et al. (nucl-th) — an LLM agent that runs viscous-hydro heavy-ion workflows end to end; the automation drumbeat reaches nuclear theory.

Deep dives

The Cross Section — Today’s Deep Dives

arXiv:2607.28396 — A measurement of the Higgs boson mass in the diphoton decay channel in proton-proton collisions at √(s)=13 TeV (CMS Collaboration)

CMS pins down m_H=125.13±0.15 GeV (±0.10 stat±0.12 syst) using the full 138 fb⁻¹ Run 2 diphoton sample — a near factor-of-two systematic reduction over their 2020 result. The key advance is the photon energy scale: rather than extrapolating electron scales from Z→ee via simulation (previously the dominant uncertainty), they now measure residual electron-photon differences directly from Z→μμγ FSR photons, and apply fine-grained E_T-dependent resolution corrections that bridge the gap between Z-electron energies (≈45 GeV) and H→γγ photons (≈60 GeV). The leading systematics are now the Z→μμγ sample statistics (74 MeV), muon momentum scale (55 MeV), and high-E_T non-linearity (54 MeV). The signal strength μ=0.95±0.06±0.07 is SM-consistent.

Why it matters: this is the most precise single-channel m_H to date, a direct input to EW global fits and vacuum-stability arguments. Combined with CMS 7+8 TeV diphoton data it gives 125.06±0.14 GeV. One visible caveat: the 13 TeV value sits 1.2σ above the earlier CMS 7+8 TeV combination, and the result remains systematics-limited, with further gains tied to the statistically starved Z→μμγ calibration sample.

arXiv:2607.27315 — The Very Nearly Right Theory of Flavor (Nima Arkani-Hamed et al.)

(Abstract only.) Arkani-Hamed et al. parametrize the ten-dimensional space of quark flavor data using “nine-link textures” — full-rank Y_u,d matrices with nine total nonzero entries and a single CP phase. Fitting all such textures, they find the CP phases cluster tightly around multiples of π/8, driven by a “Yukawa triangle” defined by the matrix entries that coincides with the unitarity triangle at leading order in small flavor parameters. The empirical observation being explained is that (α,β,γ)≈(π/2,π/8,3π/8). Crucially, the two triangles differ beyond leading order, yielding calculable deviations from these values that the next generation of unitarity-triangle-angle measurements can decisively confirm or exclude.

Why it matters: this turns a striking numerical coincidence into a falsifiable framework, and lands one day after Lin’s geometric CKM reparameterization — two independent attacks on the same pattern. A bonus: the textures are sparse with naturally real determinants, which combined with spontaneous CP violation offers a route to solving strong CP. Caveat: as abstract-only, the robustness of the “clustering” claim and the size of the predicted deviations relative to projected experimental precision cannot be assessed here.

arXiv:2607.27313 — Suppressed Quantum Effects of Weakly Coupled Waves (Yunjia Bao et al.)

Bao et al. prove two general obstructions to detecting nonclassicality in weakly coupled waves (axion DM, gravitational radiation), using the cavity haloscope as worked example. First, detectors couple not to fundamental plane-wave modes but to a coarse-grained “effective mode”; if DM occupies many independent modes, the quantum central limit theorem drives the effective-mode P-function to a nonnegative thermal Gaussian, erasing negativity regardless of occupancy. They show convergence is rapid — the purity of 𝒩 coarse-grained Fock states approaches the Gaussian value 1/(1+2n) as ∼n(n+1)/[𝒩(2n+1)²], fast even for n∼1. Second, even granting a maximally nonclassical effective mode, all nonclassicality signatures carry extra powers of the tiny conversion efficiency η=sin²⁽gt_m)∼10⁻²¹: Mandel Q_c=ηQ_a≥-η, squeezing S_c=ηS_a. Distinguishing a Fock from a coherent axion via number statistics needs N_shot∼1/η², i.e. t_int≳10¹⁷ yr — utterly impractical and unenhanced by large N_eff.

Why it matters: this is a general no-go closing off the recent high-profile “quantize gravity from GW observations” program, and the cold-water counterpart to yesterday’s Blas–Oller GW→γγ claim. Distinguishing classical states (coherent vs. Gaussian) remains feasible, needing only N_shot∼1/⟨n_c⟩². Caveat honestly flagged: the CLT can be evaded — few contributing modes (fuzzy DM, condensates), surviving inter-mode correlations, or highly monochromatic late-time sources with TΔω≲1 — though even then the η-suppression persists unless quantum resources scale as 1/η.

Citation radar

This week’s radar tilts heavily toward methods and machinery: two of the four papers are software releases (an LLM-driven phase-transition pipeline and a spectral Feynman-integral solver), and two probe early-universe or quantum-information observables. The recurring signal is that the community is rapidly citing infrastructure — agentic frameworks, transport codes — and staking positions in the fast-moving debate over primordial-black-hole formation from phase transitions.

arXiv:2606.19425 — LeWRON: Agentic Analysis of Electroweak Phase Transitions (Isaac R. Wang)

LeWRON is an LLM-agent framework that takes a BSM Lagrangian (or a literature target) and orchestrates the full electroweak-phase-transition pipeline: constructing the finite-temperature effective potential, tracking thermal histories, computing nucleation, and predicting gravitational-wave spectra. Its design leans on role-separated model calls (deterministic coding vs. reasoning agents), CAS-assisted symbolic derivations, audited Pydantic artifacts, and human checkpoints. The paper validates in “reproduction mode” (recovering the singlet-scalar nucleation temperatures of Ref. [71] to <1%, and a 2HDM+a potential) and “discovery mode” (ALP-Higgs and 2HDM+S), where it claims to improve on prior renormalization treatments.

The ~5 citations in roughly two months reflect a surge of “hep-ph agent” papers (HEPTAPOD, MadAgents, DarkAgents, Collider-Bench, all cited here) rather than physics results per se. LeWRON is positioned as the first domain-specialized agent for end-to-end EWPT analysis, and it is being cited as part of this emerging cluster establishing what agentic workflows for particle theory can do — a claim to a niche everyone in that subfield now references.

arXiv:2606.11296 — Tripartite Entanglement in e⁺e⁻ →tt̅Z (Dorival Gonçalves et al.)

No HTML rendering was available, so this entry rests on title and metadata alone. The paper studies tripartite quantum entanglement in the three-body final state tt̅Z at a future lepton collider — extending the now-active program of measuring entanglement and Bell-inequality violation in top-quark pairs to a genuinely three-party system.

With ~5 citations shortly after posting, it appears to be riding the broader wave of collider quantum-information studies that took off after entanglement was established as an observable in tt̅. Tripartite entanglement is a natural and less-explored frontier, so an early concrete proposal in the e⁺e⁻ environment plausibly serves as an anchor reference for follow-up work. Without the text I cannot verify the specific entanglement measures used or the headline sensitivity, and the citation pattern is best read as topical momentum rather than a single decisive result.

arXiv:2606.26691 — CHESS: CHEbyshev pSeudo-Spectral transport for Feynman integral differential equations (Yuanche Liu et al.)

CHESS is a Wolfram Language package for high-precision one-dimensional transport of ϵ-factorized differential equations for Feynman master integrals. Given a path-pulled-back connection B(t) — supplied either as constant-matrix/scalar-one-form data or as a direct numerical evaluator — it uses Chebyshev–Lobatto spectral collocation, solving the triangular ϵ-hierarchy sequentially with one factored node matrix acting on many right-hand sides, plus residue-based regularization of spurious endpoint singularities. Benchmarks are striking: a physical-region two-loop six-point double-pentagon reaches agreement with AMFlow at the 10⁻¹⁰¹ level; three-loop five-point families with up to 734 masters complete in under 80 s; and a fixed-protocol comparison shows 8.8–17.9× speedups over DiffExp. An elliptic non-planar-triangle example exercises the direct-matrix mode.

The ~5 citations in about a month signal a needed tool: multi-scale, high-multiplicity integral families (three-loop five-point, two-loop six-point) are exactly the current bottlenecks, and CHESS slots into the DiffExp/SeaSyde/AMFlow ecosystem with demonstrable performance gains. Its deliberately narrow scope — transport only, given a canonical basis and path — makes it easy to adopt as a drop-in propagation layer.

arXiv:2605.11332 — Reviving primordial black hole formation in slow first-order phase transitions (Wen-Yuan Ai et al.)

This paper is a direct rebuttal to recent claims that PBH formation from slow first-order phase transitions is ruled out. The problem: bubble simulations extract the density contrast in the spatially flat gauge, δ⁽F), whereas the collapse threshold is defined in comoving gauge, and δ⁽F)≃10 δ⁽C) at horizon re-entry — apparently killing the mechanism. Using a gauge-invariant treatment that avoids the superhorizon approximation, the authors confirm the suppression, but then argue the mechanism survives: if post-transition reheating is slow (Γ_ϕ< H_), the Universe enters an early matter-dominated era in which even small overdensities grow and collapse. They derive a model-independent condition (β/H_n ≲18, EMD duration ≳10³ H_⁻¹), extend Doroshkevich statistics to non-Gaussian P(δ_k), and realize the scenario in a conformal U(1)_X model yielding asteroid-mass PBHs that can be all of dark matter.

The ~5 citations since May reflect its role in a live, contested debate (Franciolini et al.; Wang et al. are the foils). A “the mechanism isn’t dead after all” paper in an active controversy naturally attracts rapid engagement from both camps.

item.title: Thursday, July 30, 2026
item.description:
A seven-sigma flavor claim and a first for FASER

The day’s sharpest result is a theory fit, not a measurement: Bhattacharya et al. arXiv:2607.27202 extend last year’s charmless B→PP SU(3)_F puzzle to B→VV and find the discrepancy with the SM SU(3)_F limit growing to above 7σ. On the experimental side, FASER posts the first LHC search for quirks arXiv:2607.26195 and ATLAS updates HH→bb̅ττ with a mild upward pull arXiv:2607.26879. Underneath, a strong lattice-gauge-theory pair and a heavy-ion methods cluster give the day real depth, and the early-universe defect thread the memory has tracked all month resurfaces with GUT-scale symmetry breaking.

Themes

Flavor SU(3) under strain

Bhattacharya et al. arXiv:2607.27202 fit B→ρK^* under isospin (acceptable), then ρ/K^* under SU(3)_F (5.2σ), then the full ρ,K^*,ϕ,ω set (>7σ). The theoretical input is deliberately minimal — group theory in the exact SU(3)_F limit — so the number is hard to wave away, though whether ~30% SU(3)-breaking rescues it is the open question they flag. This is a different corner from the b→sℓℓ/νν̅ modes the week has circled: a hadronic-amplitude anomaly, not a rare FCNC. Lin’s geometric CKM reparameterization arXiv:2607.26681 sits nearby but is far more speculative.

Non-Abelian lattice with dynamical fermions

Rouxinol et al. deliver a variational Monte Carlo treatment of the untruncated 2+1D SU(2) theory coupled to staggered fermions — a methods paper arXiv:2607.26131 and its phase-diagram application arXiv:2607.26132, mapping a magnetic-flux transition and a gauge-matter delocalization crossover along the physical coupling line. A neural-network gauge wavefunction plus a Gaussian fermionic correction gives a sign-problem-free route to continuous non-Abelian groups with matter. Ding et al.’s quenched study of static potentials under imaginary rotation arXiv:2607.26939 rounds out the lattice end.

Jets as spectroscopy of the medium

Two papers push jet-medium coupling toward genuine observables. Kurkela et al. arXiv:2607.26851 argue the angular moments of the jet wake isolate non-hydrodynamic modes — higher moments encode the collision operator’s relaxation spectrum, giving the first observable claimed to be exclusively sensitive to the non-hydro sector. Soudi et al. arXiv:2607.26143 derive an equilibrating parton shower directly from QCD effective kinetic theory that reproduces the full linearized Boltzmann equation, handling hard energy loss and thermal equilibration on equal footing.

GUT-scale defects and gravitational waves

Hemming et al. arXiv:2607.27158 simulate GUT symmetry breaking, finding biased domain walls plus monopoles with novel interactions — monopole absorption on walls, magnetically charged black holes from collapsing walls, and a biased-wall GW background. Brunelli et al. arXiv:2607.26124 get a multi-peaked high-frequency signal from multiple cosmic superstrings, and Jinno et al. arXiv:2607.26569 show rippled bubble walls resonantly enhance production of particles far heavier than the transition scale. A continuation of the defect/phase-transition GW drumbeat.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.27202 — B→VV pushes the charmless SU(3)_F discrepancy past 7σ with minimal theory input; the flavor result of the day.
  • arXiv:2607.26195 — FASER’s first-ever LHC quirk search, excluding weak-scale masses over a broad infracolor confinement range.
  • arXiv:2607.26879 — ATLAS HH→bb̅ττ: μ_HH=2.6⁺¹.4_-1.0, a modest upward pull and a tightened κ_λ interval.
  • arXiv:2607.26851 — Jet-wake angular moments as a clean probe of non-hydrodynamic QGP modes; a genuinely new observable.
  • arXiv:2607.26132 — Untruncated SU(2) with dynamical fermions solved variationally; a phase diagram from first principles.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.26739 Automated NRQCD/NRQED simulations with P-wave states — Maxia et al. (hep-ph) — MadSONS extends MadGraph to bound-state production, improving the J/ψ+ψ(2S) description of LHCb data.
  • arXiv:2607.26128 Neutrino flavor via Glashow resonance at tau air-shower telescopes — Ding et al. (hep-ph) — TAMBO/TRINITY sensitivity to ν̅_e/ν_τ, a fresh handle for the UHE-neutrino program.
  • arXiv:2607.26686 A bound on the dynamical Love number — Kehagias et al. (gr-qc) — Schwarz–Pick applied to tidal response; the f-mode model saturates it.
  • arXiv:2607.27174 Perturbing gravitational atoms — Bošković et al. (gr-qc) — negative, parametrically enhanced Love numbers for spinning boson clouds.
  • arXiv:2607.26826 Paleodetectors for Galactic stellar-collapse neutrinos — Yamasaki et al. (astro-ph.HE) — burst-like SN activity at 10 pc within reach.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.27202 — Anomalies in Hadronic B→VV Decays (Bhubanjyoti Bhattacharya et al.)

Bhattacharya et al. extend last year’s charmless B→PP SU(3)_F puzzle to the vector-vector modes, fitting HFLAV/PDG data with reduced matrix elements (equivalently topological diagrams) in the exact SU(3)_F limit, the only theoretical simplification being neglect of the small Wilson coefficients c_7,c_8 (a ~10% effect). Three fits are staged. The isospin-only B→ρK^* fit is acceptable (χ²/d.o.f.=3.6/3, p=0.31) — but forces |P_uc/P_tc|∼200, some 300× above the expected ≲0.5; imposing the physical constraint ≤1 collapses it to 4.4σ. The combined SU(3)_F fit over V∈{ρ,K^} gives 39.2/5, a 5.2σ discrepancy; adding ϕ,ω pushes it to 130/20, p<10⁻¹⁵, i.e. >7σ. The jump is driven partly by ℬ(B⁰→ϕK^0) and ℬ(B⁰→ωK^*0) (each contributing >20 to χ²) and by the failure of f_L≫f_T in the new modes sharpening tension with ΔS=1 polarization data.

If it holds, this is a hadronic-amplitude anomaly distinct from the b→sℓℓ/νν̅ FCNC anomalies — a breakdown of the SM’s flavor-symmetry structure in tree/penguin dominated decays. The result’s strength is its minimal theory input; its acknowledged vulnerability is that only exact SU(3)_F was tested. The authors concede that whether realistic ~30% SU(3)_F-breaking can absorb a 7σ gap “must be checked,” though they judge it unlikely. Robustness was verified with three independent codes and tens of thousands of seeds.

arXiv:2607.26195 — First Search for Quirks at the LHC with FASER (FASER Collaboration)

FASER delivers the first LHC quirk search, using 186 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV pp data (2022–2024). Quirks — pairs charged under a QCD-like infracolor SU(N_IC=2) with right-handed-lepton SM charges — are Drell-Yan produced forward, remain bound by an unbreakable IC string, and arrive at FASER (480 m downstream) slow and out-of-time. The signature is a pair depositing ~2 MIPs of charge in all eight scintillators with reconstructed speed 0.6<β<1 and arrival time t_0 offset from the nominal bunch. Backgrounds (through-going muons via an ABCD estimate, muon-induced “kinked” showers) total well below one event; the signal region contains zero observed events. Using a CL_s fit, masses up to 179 GeV are excluded at Λ=10 keV, and for the first time weak-scale quirk masses are excluded across the broad range 300 eV<Λ<100 keV.

This opens a genuinely new frontier: non-Abelian hidden sectors (motivated by neutral naturalness and IC-glueball dark matter) had no prior dedicated LHC search, only the DØ Tevatron limit. FASER’s forward, low-background geometry turns the quirks’ slowness into a clean discriminant. Caveats are honest and intrinsic: only ~0.03–0.04% of produced quirks reach the fiducial region, with reconstruction/selection efficiency ~1% (10%) at m_𝒬=50 (175) GeV, and the signal normalization carries a ~25% ISR/FSR modeling uncertainty (up to 28% simulation-statistics uncertainty at small Λ). This is half of Run 3, so reach will grow.

arXiv:2607.26879 — Improved HH→bb̅τ⁺τ⁻ Analysis with 196 fb⁻¹ (ATLAS) (ATLAS Collaboration)

(Abstract only.) ATLAS updates its non-resonant di-Higgs search in bb̅ττ, combining 140 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV with 56 fb⁻¹ at 13.6 TeV plus reconstruction and analysis improvements. The signal strength is μ_HH=2.6⁺¹.4_-1.0, an observed (expected) significance of 2.6 (1.2)σ over background-only, and 1.65σ above the SM prediction — a mild upward pull consistent with the SM. The self-coupling modifier is constrained to κ_λ∈[-3.4,1.6]∪[5.5,10.1] observed ([-1.7,8.5] expected) at 95% CL. As validation, ZH and ZZ in the same final state are measured at 3.5 (2.4)σ and 1.8 (2.7)σ respectively.

The result advances the HH program incrementally: the tightened κ_λ interval sharpens the constraint on the Higgs potential, while the ~2.5× SM central value continues a pattern of slight excesses in this channel worth tracking as Run 3 statistics accumulate. The excess is modest — the SM lies comfortably within 1.65σ — so no anomaly is claimed. The validation channels demonstrate the method’s control, though the observed ZH pull sits above expectation and ZZ below, indicating the measurements remain statistics-limited.

item.title: Wednesday, July 29, 2026
item.description:
Galactic neutrinos and electroweak photons

The day’s weight sits on two clean observations at opposite scales. IceCube establishes high-energy neutrino emission from the Milky Way’s plane at 5.7σ using all three flavor morphologies over 12 years (arXiv:2607.25966) — the Galactic diffuse signal, now robustly in hand and feeding the multi-messenger machinery the week’s UHE-neutrino tension papers have been circling. At the LHC, ATLAS observes electroweak γγjj production at 6.2σ (arXiv:2607.25869), extending the electroweak-boson program that ran through last week’s WZjj polarization and ZZ work, and casting the result in dimension-8 aQGC limits. Around these, a cluster of early-universe simulation-code releases and a scattering of flavor/CP methods.

Themes

Electroweak boson production and quartic couplings

ATLAS’s γγjj observation arXiv:2607.25869 lands slightly below the SM cross section (13.8 vs 17.1 fb) and sets aQGC bounds — the same dim-8 EFT language the memory has flagged as the default for VBS-adjacent searches. Yilmaz et al. arXiv:2607.25935 project ZZγ aQGC reach at FCC-hh an order of magnitude past current LHC limits, and ATLAS’s Run 2 large-radius jet calibration arXiv:2607.25893 (1% JES/JMS to 1 TeV) is the enabling infrastructure for the boosted end.

Galactic neutrino astronomy

Beyond the 5.7σ plane detection, IceCube arXiv:2607.25966 finds the inner Galaxy a prominent source — 217 shower events above 5 TeV against 154 expected. This is the constructive counterpart to the week’s UHE-neutrino anomaly (the 7.5σ ANITA/KM3NeT-vs-IceCube tension): the diffuse Galactic component is exactly what those joint fits assume as background.

Early-universe simulation tooling

Three code-facing entries. CosmoLattice 2.0 arXiv:2607.24978 adds non-minimal gravity couplings, axion-gauge sectors, defect-network initial conditions and O(10) GPU speedups; TempLat arXiv:2607.24908 is a performance-portable Kokkos-based lattice engine powering that release. Dankovsky et al. arXiv:2607.25073 use CosmoLattice to fix the spurious IR wiggles in domain-wall GW spectra — directly relevant to the NANOGrav-band defect thread that has run all month.

Flavor and CP probes

Belle/Belle II post the first search for B⁰→K⁰_Sτ⁺τ⁻ arXiv:2607.25607, ℬ<8.3×10⁻⁴, tightening the B→Kττ combination — a new corner of the b→s program. Heuser et al. arXiv:2607.25764 show, via a dispersive method, that LHCb’s large localized CP asymmetry in B^±→K^±π⁺π⁻ is driven by suppression of the CP-conserving part, not an enhancement. And Lamba et al. build a quantum-information framework for CP violation in tt̅, split across production arXiv:2607.25029 and tomography arXiv:2607.25034.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.25966 — IceCube’s 5.7σ Galactic-plane neutrino emission with all-flavor morphology; a genuine milestone for Galactic multi-messenger astronomy.
  • arXiv:2607.25869 — ATLAS observes EW γγjj at 6.2σ, with dim-8 aQGC interpretation; the electroweak program’s next channel.
  • arXiv:2607.24930 — Blas et al. argue coherent GWs decay into photon pairs, a purely quantum (∝N²) effect, and derive first CMB/photofission constraints — a surprising new handle worth a read.
  • arXiv:2607.25607 — Belle/Belle II’s first B⁰→K⁰_Sτ⁺τ⁻ search; a fresh b→sττ limit.
  • arXiv:2607.24933 — Lin et al.’s solvable 1D lattice model pins down exactly what separates coherent from incoherent sub-GeV DM-nucleus scattering: crystal-momentum conservation, fading as multiphonons grow.

From the community

Watson’s history of high-energy neutrino and cosmic-ray detector construction from 1980–2000 arXiv:2607.25535 — DUMAND, Baikal, IceCube and Auger, with candor about the difficulties and the role the (retracted) Cygnus X-3 PeV claims played. A fitting companion to today’s IceCube result.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.24928 Bound-state beta decay of tritium — Akhmedov et al. (hep-ph) — a novel Doppler-based route to direct neutrino mass and sterile searches.
  • arXiv:2607.25653 Fragmentation of jets containing Υ(nS) — CMS Collaboration (hep-ex) — MC quarkonium-in-parton-shower modeling found unsatisfactory.
  • arXiv:2607.24935 Top-quark mass interpretation from top-flavoured mesons — Corcella et al. (hep-ph) — the pole-mass ambiguity pinned at 200–300 MeV, order Λ_QCD.
  • arXiv:2607.25606 Virtual state and two-pole structure of Ξ(1690)/Ξ(1820) — He (hep-ph) — a Λ(1405)-like two-pole reading from BESIII data.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.25966 — High-energy neutrino emission from the Milky Way (R. Abbasi et al.)

Abstract only. Combining all three neutrino-flavor event morphologies with updated ice modelling, calibration and reconstruction over 12 years of IceCube data, a predefined global analysis establishes high-energy neutrino emission from the Galactic plane at 5.7σ. A follow-up study identifies the inner Galaxy as a prominent source: 217 shower events above 5 TeV visible energy against an expected background of 154.4 ± 4.1. The multi-flavor approach is what pushes this over the discovery threshold — earlier IceCube plane hints leaned on cascades alone.

Why it matters: this is the constructive counterpart to the week’s UHE-neutrino tension thread. The diffuse Galactic component is precisely the background assumed in the ANITA/KM3NeT-vs-IceCube joint fits, so having it in hand at >5σ tightens those interpretations while opening Galactic multi-messenger astronomy — cosmic-ray propagation and neutrino properties probed over kiloparsec baselines. As an abstract-only entry, the systematic treatment of the diffuse-emission modelling (which sets whether the inner-Galaxy excess is source-like or propagation-driven) can’t be assessed here.

arXiv:2607.25869 — Observation of electroweak γγjj production at 13 TeV in 140 fb⁻¹ with ATLAS (ATLAS Collaboration)

Abstract only. ATLAS observes the electroweak production of two isolated photons plus two jets at 6.2σ, with a fiducial cross section of 13.8⁺³.0_-2.6 fb, sitting below but consistent with the SM prediction of 17.1 ±2.4 fb. Fiducial and differential cross sections are measured for both the EW-only and combined QCD+EW γγjj processes, and the data are interpreted in EFT, setting limits on several dimension-8 Wilson coefficients parameterising anomalous quartic gauge couplings.

Why it matters: this extends the ATLAS electroweak-boson program — following recent WZjj polarization and ZZ work — into a new VBS-adjacent channel, using the same dim-8 aQGC language that is now the default for these searches (and the framework Yilmaz et al. project forward to FCC-hh). The measured central value ~20% below SM is within the ~2 fb uncertainties, so no tension, but the modest downward pull is the kind of thing differential distributions and more data will need to pin down.

arXiv:2607.24930 — Gravitational waves decay in vacuum: a low-energy effect of quantized gravitation (Diego Blas et al.)

Blas and Oller argue that GWs, treated as coherent graviton states rather than classical fields, decay into photon pairs via graviton fusion (gg→γγ, Skobelev amplitude) — a process forbidden classically and semiclassically, vanishing as ħ→0, and enhanced by the graviton number squared N². The key technical point (Supplement SA): the coherent-state mode cannot propagate in the internal graviton line because momentum conservation forces it on-shell at s=0, where the derivative coupling vanishes. The radiated power scales as W_γ∝G² E_rel²ω_s²σ_ω², giving a compact form W_γ=350π(r_m/ℓ)²ħω². They derive first constraints on recurrent GW populations from CMB μ/y distortions (COBE/FIRAS: |μ|<9×10⁻⁵, |y|<1.5×10⁻⁵), UV/X-ray and γ-ray backgrounds, and D/⁴He photofission, all cast as bounds on √(Γ) ϵE_rel/M_⊙ vs ω_s.

Why it matters: a genuinely new, purely quantum-gravitational handle on GW sources, whose detection would evidence quantized gravity. The honest caveat is front and center: for astrophysical binaries the photon luminosity is minuscule (comparable to Hawking radiation of the equivalent mass, number luminosity ∼10⁶ s⁻¹ at merger), and SGWB depletion is negligible (∼10⁻¹¹⁰ m⁻³s⁻¹; |Φ|≈10⁻²⁵ Hz⁻¹ to the GUT scale). Only in ultralight-dark-matter scenarios, where huge occupation numbers boost gg↔ϕϕ, do rates reach ∼10⁵⁴ s⁻¹ — and that requires the exotic light-scalar sector to exist.

item.title: Tuesday, July 28, 2026
item.description:
Flavor precision, detectors gone solar

The day’s weight sits on flavor. BESIII posts its best-precision measurement of D→πℓ⁺ν across all four charge/lepton modes (arXiv:2607.23945, arXiv:2607.23949), pinning f_+^D→π(0)|V_cd| to sub-percent and testing e/μ universality; and Allwicher et al. arXiv:2607.24494 give the NA62 golden-mode measurement its next interpretive turn, translating K⁺→π⁺νν̅ into constraints on B→Kνν̅ and B_s→μμ — the cross-mode phenomenology the memory has tracked since the kaon result anchored the week. CMS adds a substantial off-shell Higgs analysis (arXiv:2607.23352). The other genuinely coherent cluster is quieter and newer: direct-detection experiments repurposed as solar-neutrino observatories.

Themes

Flavor precision, kaons to charm

Allwicher et al. arXiv:2607.24494 is the direct continuation of the NA62 thread that has run all month (Blanke et al. on KOTO II room, then the lattice R_e/μ benchmark): under different flavor assumptions the K⁺ result now feeds B→Kνν̅, B_s→μμ, and forecasts for K_L→π⁰νν̅. Independently, BESIII’s D→πℓν (arXiv:2607.23945) delivers |V_cd| and the form factor at record precision plus first forward-backward asymmetries, with a null scalar-current search — clean, and SM-consistent. Two rungs of the CKM ladder tightened on the same day.

Direct detection as a solar-neutrino observatory

A real coalescence. Amaral et al. release SNuDD arXiv:2607.22817, an open code for solar-neutrino rates at xenon detectors, and set NSI limits from LZ/XENONnT/PandaX-4T already approaching dedicated-experiment reach. Beccaria et al. arXiv:2607.24584 use the newly observed CEνNS signal in those same detectors to bound invisible ν_2 decay, competitive with SNO. Han et al. arXiv:2607.24421 supply the sub-percent flux framework (Earth-matter MSW, time-varying baseline) such measurements now need. The neutrino floor has become a physics program.

Hubble tension and where the neutrino mass hides

Roy Choudhury arXiv:2607.24443 pushes a 1.1%-precision distance-ladder H_0=73.3, a 6.85σ tension that the corrected Pantheon+/DES-DOVEKIE reanalysis does not soften — the counterpoint to last week’s “walls against tension-solvers.” Qu et al. arXiv:2607.24742 make the complementary move: deconstructing which probes drive the ∑m_ν<0.056 eV bound and building a late-Universe-free route that relaxes it to <0.41 eV, trading statistical power for dark-energy independence and landing near Project 8’s target.

Tooling: agents, scaling laws, symbolic fits

The automation thread from yesterday continues with Diefenbacher et al.’s agentic SFitter re-casting arXiv:2607.22813. Alongside it, Uslu et al. arXiv:2607.23377 show jet-foundation-model performance is forecastable — a scaling law that predicts a 100×-larger model’s loss to one percent — and Granger et al. arXiv:2607.24710 use symbolic regression to extract a closed-form nonperturbative TMD from Drell-Yan data.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.23945 — BESIII’s best-to-date D→πℓν: record |V_cd|, first forward-backward asymmetries, null scalar current, LFU intact.
  • arXiv:2607.23352 — CMS off-shell Higgs: Γ_H=5.1⁺².0_-1.8 MeV, first off-shell self-coupling and compositeness (Λ_H>870 GeV) constraints.
  • arXiv:2607.24494 — The NA62 result propagated into B-physics: Allwicher et al. turn one kaon branching ratio into a handle on b→s new physics.
  • arXiv:2607.24584 — First invisible-solar-neutrino-decay bound from CEνNS, already rivaling SNO — the direct-detection-as-neutrino-probe theme with a concrete limit.
  • arXiv:2607.24587 — First nonperturbative constraint on the gluon Collins-Soper kernel from lattice QCD; EIC-facing groundwork.

From the community

Abe arXiv:2607.24179 floats a gravity-aligned vertical e⁺e⁻ linear collider in a 3 km shaft reusing the KEK complex — a deliberately concept-level provocation amid the Higgs-factory cost debate. And Razzaghi arXiv:2607.24670 is an unusual epistemics-of-technology essay arguing neutrinos are “epistemically mature yet operationally resistant,” with a proposed operability index.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.24203 Prospects for η_t→W⁺W⁻ at the HL-LHC — Yang et al. (hep-ph) — a b-jet-free dilepton channel for the freshly observed toponium.
  • arXiv:2607.24329 Ultraviolet boundary condition and the Higgs mass — Guo et al. (hep-ph) — λ(M_P)=0 gives m_h=122.0 GeV at full two loops, 2.6% low.
  • arXiv:2607.24448 Dark Matter Searches with Sodium Iodide Detectors — Martinez et al. (hep-ex) — a review of the DAMA-replication landscape.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.23945 — Precision measurements of D⁰→π⁻ℓ⁺ν_ℓ and D⁺→π⁰ℓ⁺ν_ℓ (ℓ=e,μ) (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

Using 20.3 fb⁻¹ at √(s)=3.773 GeV and the double-tag technique, BESIII measures all four D→πℓν modes to record precision. The branching fractions land at (2.950±0.017±0.017)×10⁻³, (2.817±0.037±0.019)×10⁻³, (3.622±0.034±0.018)×10⁻³, and (3.507±0.043±0.026)×10⁻³ for the π⁻e, π⁻μ, π⁰e, π⁰μ channels respectively — a factor 2–3 improvement over the previous BESIII results, which are superseded. A simultaneous fit of partial rates in ten q² bins yields f_+^D→π(0)|V_cd|=0.1425±0.0005±0.0003 (sub-percent), giving |V_cd|=0.2262±0.0008±0.0005±0.0018_LQCD or f_+^D→π(0)=0.6339±0.0024±0.0014 depending on which external input is assumed. First forward-backward asymmetries are extracted, and a first scalar-current search gives Re(C_S^μ)=0.022±0.023±0.003, consistent with zero.

Why it matters: this tightens one rung of the CKM ladder (c→d) on the same day the digest highlights kaon-to-B propagation, and the null scalar current directly constrains the two-Higgs-doublet/leptoquark scenarios invoked for the b→c LFU anomalies — here in a clean, SM-consistent charm transition. LFU is tested via μ/e rate ratios across q². Caveat: the |V_cd| extraction is now dominated by the lattice form-factor uncertainty (±0.0018_LQCD versus ±0.0008 statistical), so further gains require theory, not more data.

arXiv:2607.23352 — Off-shell Higgs boson measurements: Yukawa couplings, self-coupling, compositeness, and width (CMS Collaboration)

(Abstract only.) CMS analyzes off-shell Higgs production in the four-lepton channel with 138 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV, combining H→ZZ and H→WW to extract Γ_H=5.1⁺².0_-1.8 MeV and exclude the no-off-shell hypothesis at >5σ. The analysis delivers several firsts: a direct test of composite-Higgs models with Λ_H>870 GeV at 95% CL, the first off-shell constraint on the Higgs self-coupling, and — combined with on-shell data — the tightest light-quark Yukawa limits to date while relaxing the usual bound on the HVV coupling for more model-independent width results.

Why it matters: the off-shell region breaks the coupling-vs-width degeneracy that plagues on-shell rate measurements, and folding in BSM loop content and modified vector couplings makes the Γ_H determination more robust than earlier off-shell extractions. The compositeness and self-coupling handles are novel uses of the same dataset. Caveat: no methodological detail is available beyond the abstract, so assumptions behind the model-independence claims cannot be assessed here.

arXiv:2607.24494 — Implications of K→πνν̅ for new physics in B decays (Lukas Allwicher et al.)

Allwicher and Bordone propagate the new NA62 ℬ(K⁺→π⁺νν̅)=9.6⁺¹.9_-1.8×10⁻¹¹ (sub-20% precision) into two BSM frameworks. In the modified-Z-coupling scenario, under Minimal Flavor Violation B_s→μμ dominates the constraints, while under Partial Compositeness the kaon mode becomes the sharpest handle on right-handed couplings δg_R — even resolving a two-fold solution that B→Kνν̅ then breaks. Both give effective NP scales Λ^Z_eff≳8 TeV, tree-level accessible at HL-LHC. In the alternative U(2)⁵ semileptonic fit with third-generation dominance (Λ_eff≳1.8 TeV), the more precise NA62 value now admits an ϵ∼0 / C_ℓq⁻∼0 SM-like solution at 68%, though in mild tension with R_D⁽) and B→K⁽)νν̅; the preferred large-BSM branch predicts ℬ(K_L→π⁰νν̅)/ℬ(K⁺→π⁺νν̅)∼1.5 (normalized to SM), within the Grossman–Nir bound.

Why it matters: this is exactly the cross-mode phenomenology the digest has tracked since the NA62 result — one kaon branching ratio now feeds correlated predictions for B→K⁽*)νν̅, B_s→μμ, and future K_L→π⁰νν̅ (KOTO II). The framework makes K_L a genuine prediction, testable by combining projected NA62 (15%), KOTO-II (25%), and Belle II (8%) precision. Caveat: the persistent B⁺→K⁺νν̅ central value sits above all predictions, and the two green fit lobes remain equally allowed at current precision — conclusions hinge on which branch nature picks.

item.title: Monday, July 27, 2026
item.description:
Lattice precision, and code that writes itself

Two currents carry the day. The first is precision lattice: Boyle et al. arXiv:2607.22358 deliver the first lattice QCD+QED calculation of the structure-dependent radiative correction to the π and K lepton-universality ratios R_e/μ — the exact input PIONEER and NA62 need to interpret their measurements. The second is the automation thread the memory has tracked since LQCDMaster: two more papers hand LLM agents the keyboard, this time for amplitude computation and full SMEFT collider pipelines. Around them, ATLAS reports evidence for boosted H→ττ (arXiv:2607.22193) and Auger sharpens the muon puzzle into a concrete demand on hadronic interactions (arXiv:2607.22323).

Themes

Agents at the console

Gu et al. arXiv:2607.21629 treat scattering amplitudes as programs and let coding agents search over analytic representations, reporting an 805× speed-up on a scored grid and matrix-element engines that close the gap to compiled MadGraph. Guo et al.’s SMEFT-Pheno-Agent arXiv:2607.22331 wraps the whole MadGraph/Pythia/Delphes chain in a natural-language agent with locked configs and audit manifests. This is the next step past LQCDMaster (July 17): agents no longer just checking work but orchestrating it, with reproducibility as the explicit selling point. Dax et al.’s SBI review arXiv:2607.21702 and the LHCb topological-trigger decorrelation study arXiv:2607.22281 round out the ML end.

Lattice precision, from LFU to the thermal medium

Beyond Boyle et al.’s R_e/μ, the lattice cluster spans the QGP: Bala et al. arXiv:2607.21729 extract non-perturbatively, for the first time, the imaginary part of the spin-dependent heavy-quark potential — different for pseudoscalar vs. vector charmonium. Hoffmann et al. arXiv:2607.22346 build a finite-temperature quantization condition for two-particle scattering via thermoparticles. Separately, Mendizabal Morentin et al. arXiv:2607.22390 fit top mass, α_s, the weak mixing angle and PDFs simultaneously in xFitter — a global-interpretation template.

EFT recasts as the default language

Two more weak-scale searches get read through EFT, as the memory flagged this becoming standard. Duarte et al. arXiv:2607.21711 recast a CMS same-sign-dimuon heavy-neutrino search into the first exclusion limits on the agnostic νSMEFT parameter space. Brivio et al. arXiv:2607.21712 study ALP pair production, including the previously unanalyzed non-resonant gg→aa four-photon channel, and reinterpret an ATLAS Higgs-resonant search in three-parameter space.

Topological defects and their waves

Yamada arXiv:2607.21701 simulates global ℤ_N string networks with baryon-vertex junctions, finding scaling (not frustration) and Ω_GW∝μ²⁽N²⁻¹⁾² for N≲8. Kanda et al. arXiv:2607.22481 show global-monopole annihilation emits Nambu-Goldstone bosons peaking at horizon scale, with a pNG dark-matter estimate. A quiet continuation of the defect-network thread that has run through July.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.22358 — First lattice QCD+QED SD correction to R_e/μ for π and K; the SM benchmark PIONEER/NA62 will quote.
  • arXiv:2607.22193 — ATLAS evidence (3.8σ) for boosted H→ττ above 300 GeV, with dedicated di-τ reconstruction.
  • arXiv:2607.21629 — Amplitude optimization as self-evolving program search; 805× speed-ups and a genuinely new take on generator internals.
  • arXiv:2607.22323 — Auger maps its X_max deficit at √(s)≃100 TeV onto a demanded 2.8–4.6× amplification of hadronic energy fraction — the muon puzzle, quantified.
  • arXiv:2607.22390 — First simultaneous NNLO fit of PDFs, top mass, α_s and the weak mixing angle, with SMEFT operators — a global-interpretation blueprint.

From the community

Scomparin’s overview of the CERN SPS fixed-target future arXiv:2607.22328 lays out the NA61 and newly approved NA60+/DiCE program for finite-μ_B QGP studies — a facility-roadmap contribution amid the ongoing strategy discussions.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.22102 Updated E141 constraints on a long-lived X_17 vector boson — Celentano et al. (hep-ph) — a refined recast that tightens the tension with ATOMKI’s preliminary lifetime.
  • arXiv:2607.22497 Dilatonic states, phase transitions, and criticality in holography — Elander et al. (hep-th) — first holographic examples of a parametrically light dilaton near a critical point.
  • arXiv:2607.22507 Born cross section for e⁺e⁻→K_S⁰Ξ̅⁺Σ⁻ — BESIII (hep-ex) — no charmonium-like signal; isospin ratio ≈1.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.22358 — First Lattice QCD Determination of Lepton-Flavor-Universality Ratios in Light-Meson Leptonic Decays (Peter Boyle et al.)

(abstract only) Boyle et al. deliver the first lattice QCD+QED calculation of the structure-dependent (SD) radiative correction to R_e/μ — the electron-to-muon leptonic-width ratio — for both π and K, working at the physical pion mass and in the continuum limit. Using the infinite-volume reconstruction method with Coulomb-gauge photons to suppress statistical noise and finite-volume effects, they obtain SM predictions R_e/μ^π= 1.23501(10)×10⁻⁴ and R_e/μ^K = 2.47653(34)×10⁻⁵ — sub-permille precision on the previously dominant hadronic uncertainty.

Why it matters: R_e/μ is a benchmark LFU test, and the O(0.1%) SD correction was the limiting theory input as PIONEER and NA62 push toward matching precision. This calculation supplies exactly that ingredient from first principles, replacing model-dependent estimates. It is the SM number those experiments will now quote against. As an abstract-only entry, the systematic budget of the continuum/QED extrapolations isn’t visible here, but the quoted errors already sit well below current experimental sensitivity.

arXiv:2607.22193 — Boosted H→ττ cross-section measurements with ATLAS (ATLAS Collaboration)

(abstract only) ATLAS reports evidence for Higgs production at p_T^H > 300 GeV in the di-hadronic-τ final state, combining full Run 2 (140 fb⁻¹, 13 TeV) with a partial Run 3 sample (162 fb⁻¹, 13.6 TeV). Standard hadronic-τ reconstruction loses efficiency when the two τs collapse into a single large-radius jet, so the analysis deploys dedicated boosted di-τ reconstruction and identification plus multivariate discriminants. The inclusive boosted measurement reaches observed (expected) significance of 3.8 (3.3)σ — evidence-level.

Why it matters: this extends H→ττ sensitivity into a high-p_T regime that probes the Higgs coupling structure and is sensitive to BSM contributions that grow with momentum transfer. Results are cast in the simplified-template-cross-section framework, with differential p_T^H measurements for gluon fusion and an inclusive VBF cross section — directly usable for EFT interpretation. The observed significance modestly exceeds expectation, consistent with SM within the still-limited boosted statistics.

arXiv:2607.21629 — Scattering Amplitudes as Programs: Self-Evolving Search for Theory and Event Generation (Yi Gu et al.)

Gu and Krippendorf treat amplitude evaluation as a program-search problem: a repository-scale coding agent (OpenAI Codex) acts as mutation operator inside an external generate–evaluate–select loop with frozen correctness gates and objectives, evolving executable amplitude programs. Three benchmarks. (1) Scaling: from a BCFW seed, search rediscovers Berends–Giele currents, then CSW, then a fixed-k split-helicity transfer dynamic program with O(n) source work, hitting an 805× geometric-mean speed-up over 34 timing cells. (2) Structural: NMHV rational forms are reorganised into R-invariant-style cells and glued supercells, lifting a cancellation-conditioning score from 0.376 to 0.605 and collapsing 8–13 terms to 2–3. (3) Tree complexity: across twenty QCD/EW processes, exact arithmetic falls 47.7× (geometric mean 11.68×), with a 5.9× post-hoc Python runtime gain. In matched pure-gluon tests (n=4→6), the evolved engine’s lead over a Sherpa-Comix exact-sum call grows 10×→277×, while its gap to -O3-compiled MadGraph Fortran narrows 77.7×→13.7×. Total cost: 115 candidates, ~$112, 8.15 agent-hours.

Why it matters: with HL-LHC projections assigning ~20% of ATLAS CPU to event generation, matrix-element kernels are a real bottleneck, and this shows agent-driven search can traverse genuine changes of representation — not just tuning — with fully archived, inspectable lineages. This is the digest’s “agents orchestrating” thread made concrete. Caveats are stated plainly: these are tree-level, single-stack, isolated-kernel benchmarks; the Comix comparison targets exact colour/helicity sums (Comix can sample), no symbolic divisibility proof accompanies the gluing, and native generator integration plus end-to-end throughput remain untested.

item.title: Friday, July 24, 2026
item.description:
Tension solutions hit two walls

The day’s coherent weight is cosmological, and it runs against the tension-solvers rather than for them. Two independent papers close off room for raising H_0: Poulin et al. arXiv:2607.20635 show that the primordial-deuterium discrepancy grows to ∼3σ precisely in the early-dark-energy models that were supposed to help, while Sabogal et al. arXiv:2607.21244 erect a percent-level “shape wall” against late-time modifications independent of the known normalization wall. That’s the natural next beat after last week’s H_0 World Cup verdict — the referees are now poking holes in the winners. The other genuine milestone is LHCb’s demonstration of real-time processing at 32 Tbps arXiv:2607.21492, the direct descendant of the July 17 GPU-Kalman-filter work.

Themes

New walls for the Hubble tension

Poulin et al. arXiv:2607.20635 find that using the CMB baryon density, standard BBN sits in ∼2σ tension with the latest deuterium measurement — worsening to 3σ under EDE, which they resolve only by invoking a very early dark-energy component (ΔH/H≃0.087 during deuterium burning), reading it as a hint of yet another light scalar. Sabogal et al. arXiv:2607.21244 show late-time E(z) modifications can raise H_0 by at most ∼2% against the required ∼8%. Both sharpen, rather than solve, the picture the World Cup left; da Silva Pereira et al.’s O(3) no-scale interacting-DE model arXiv:2607.20320 is the model-building counterpoint targeting DESI’s phantom crossing.

Dark matter across sources and thresholds

A varied cluster. Bisal et al. arXiv:2607.20588 show that NLO corrections push pure-Higgsino–nucleon scattering below the neutrino floor over swaths of MSSM space — a genuine blind spot for direct detection. Alloni et al. arXiv:2607.21363 repurpose RES-NOVA’s archaeological-lead bolometers for solar axions, extending the July 22 inelastic-DM work to a multi-coupling probe, while Ge et al. arXiv:2607.21168 use the Sun’s 5.5 MeV fusion line to make MeV electrophilic ALPs detectable at LZ/PandaX. Kozynets et al. arXiv:2607.20620 develop Earth-shielding daily modulation to disentangle electron vs. nuclear couplings.

Proton spin and momentum

Alexandrou et al. arXiv:2607.21230 deliver a continuum-limit lattice determination at physical masses showing both the momentum (⟨x_N⟩=0.995) and spin (J_N=0.507) sum rules are satisfied — a clean confirmation, paired with Hatta’s pedagogical overview arXiv:2607.20761 of the Jaffe-Manohar vs. Ji decompositions. This continues the structure thread that ran through July 23’s gravitational form factors.

Real-time data and detector hardware

LHCb’s converged architecture arXiv:2607.21492 processes the full 32 Tbps in real time with off-the-shelf networking and a GPU filter — the highest throughput in any experiment, and the production endpoint of this month’s real-time-reconstruction wave. Kolevatov et al. arXiv:2607.20831 demonstrate SQUID readout of a high-Q LC resonator for the DMRadio axion program.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.21492 — LHCb processes 32 Tbps in real time on off-the-shelf hardware; a new throughput standard for the field.
  • arXiv:2607.20635 — Poulin et al. argue an emerging BBN deuterium discrepancy points to very early dark energy — and worsens under the EDE fixes for H_0.
  • arXiv:2607.21244 — The “shape wall”: late-time H_0 solutions capped at ∼2%, independent of the normalization wall.
  • arXiv:2607.21230 — Lattice at physical masses in the continuum: proton momentum and spin sum rules both close.
  • arXiv:2607.20588 — Higgsino–nucleon scattering driven below the neutrino floor by NLO cancellations — a direct-detection blind spot.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.20608 Earth rotation turns event timing into a geometric probe of UHE neutrino origin — Cheek et al. (hep-ph) — timing disfavors (p≃0.13) but doesn’t exclude a DM-decay origin for KM3-230213A; a follow-up to July 23’s UHE fit.
  • arXiv:2607.20825 The supernumerary K(1690) from COMPASS as a strange hybrid — Chen et al. (hep-ph) — reads COMPASS’s third pseudoscalar K as a 0⁻ hybrid, extending the July 21 spin-exotic thread to strangeness.
  • arXiv:2607.21252 Thermal Resummation for Very Strong First-order Phase Transitions — Klose (hep-ph) — 2PI techniques for the regime where the high-T expansion breaks down; the constructive side of the daisy-resummation debate.
  • arXiv:2607.20718 The Well-Tempered Likelihood — Nachman et al. (stat.ME) — GOF-normalized confidence intervals that self-limit under model misspecification; a usable fix for overconfident fits.
  • arXiv:2607.21586 Four-loop gauge coupling beta functions in the SM — Bezuglov et al. (hep-ph) — a precision building block.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.21492 — A converged architecture for processing 32 Tbps of physics data in real-time at the LHCb experiment (Roel Aaij et al.)

The upgraded LHCb now reads out its entire detector — roughly 30 MHz of non-empty pp collisions, 32 Tbps — with no hardware low-level trigger, a factor-40 increase in data rate over the previous system. The engineering result: the full stream is filtered in real time on just 164 nodes (2× AMD EPYC 7502, 2× NVIDIA RTX A5000 each), applying a 30:1 reduction in HLT1 entirely on GPU. The design rests on three moves: commercial-off-the-shelf networking (an InfiniBand HDR fat-tree treating event-building as an all-to-all personalized exchange), second-scale host-memory buffering that eliminates incast without deep-buffer switches, and a “converged” node hosting readout, event-building, and GPU filtering together via zero-copy/RDMA. Algorithmically, a multi-event GPU scheduler batches ~600–800 events per sequence, with mixed-precision reconstruction (single precision for a truncated-region Kalman filter; half precision for VELO storage and SciFi seeding). They report 41 MHz peak combined throughput, 36% headroom over the 30 MHz requirement, and demonstrate a full EB+HLT1 integration test sustaining 160 GB/s memory and 115 GB/s PCIe per node with no performance drops.

Why it matters: this is the production endpoint of the month’s real-time-reconstruction wave (the July 17 GPU-Kalman work), and the comparison table makes the claim concrete — the highest software-processed data rate of any experiment, exceeding ATLAS/CMS (1.6 Tbps into software after a 300× L1 cut) and ALICE (7.2 Tbps). Removing the low-level trigger reduces selection bias by considering the whole event. It’s an engineering demonstration paper rather than a physics measurement; the throughput figures are commissioning-phase benchmarks.

arXiv:2607.20635 — What could an emerging Big Bang Nucleosynthesis discrepancy be hinting at? (Vivian Poulin et al.)

Using PRIMAT (rewritten in Python) with the Cooke et al. deuterium measurement (10⁵D/H = 2.527±0.030), the BBN-inferred baryon density ω_b ≃ 0.0219 sits ~2.1σ below the ΛCDM CMB value and ~3.1σ below the higher ω_b = 0.02272±0.00014 preferred in EDE fits — early-dark-energy solutions to H₀ generically raise ω_b and thus worsen the deuterium problem. The authors test three expansion histories against the EDE ω_b target: ΛCDM, a ΔN_eff extension, and a transient “very early dark energy” (vEDE) component peaking during deuterium burning. Constant extra radiation fails (Q_DMAP = 3.1σ, ΔAIC ≃ +1.2): it raises Y_p too efficiently at weak freeze-out. vEDE succeeds, because a boost localized at T_D ≃ 0.03 MeV shortens the residual deuterium-burning window (raising D/H at large ω_b) while barely touching ⁴He synthesis. The combined fit gives ΔH/H(T_D) = 0.087⁺⁰·⁰³⁶₋₀.₀₃₇, no residual tension (Q_DMAP = 0.7σ, ΔAIC ≃ −5.3).

Why it matters: this is the natural referee’s-follow-up to the H₀ World Cup — the very models that win on H₀ lose on primordial deuterium, and the resolution demands yet another light scalar, framed as an axiverse window at the BBN epoch. Caveats are candidly stated: the CMB is compressed to a single Gaussian ω_b likelihood (not a joint fit); nuclear-rate uncertainties enter only through tabulated MC errors; the discrepancy is partly rate-driven (PArthENoPE agrees better with the data), and the updated D/H = 2.508 softens the ΛCDM tension to 2.7σ.

arXiv:2607.21244 — Hubble tension: the shape wall (Miguel A. Sabogal et al.)

The standard no-go against late-time H₀ solutions is a normalization wall (BAO fixes r_d·H₀). This paper erects an independent shape wall: at fixed acoustic scale θ_s and sound horizon, δH₀/H₀ ≃ δI/I, where I ≡ ∫dz/E(z). Using Gaussian-process reconstructions of the dimensionless expansion rate E(z) from unanchored SNeIa (PantheonPlus, DESY5Dvk, Union3) and DESI DR2 BAO — marginalizing over the r_d·h amplitude to retain only shape information — they find E(z) can deviate at most ≈5–7% from fiducial ΛCDM. The directly-constrained low-redshift integral I_< (z ≲ 2.3) is pinned to the percent level: δI_</I_< ≲ 0.5% (68%), ≲1.5% (95%) across SNeIa+BAO combinations, mapping to (δH₀/H₀)_< ≲ 0.8% at 95%. Adding a model-guided estimate of the unconstrained high-z tail I_> (from ΛCDM/wCDM fits) yields a total δH₀/H₀ ≲ 2% (conservative) to ≲3.7% (maximally permissive) — versus the ≈9.3% needed to close the tension, leaving ≳4.3σ residual.

Why it matters: alongside Poulin et al., this is the day’s second wall against tension-solvers, and it is statistically stronger than the normalization wall since it survives redshift-independent BAO recalibration. The key methodological point — pointwise E(z) envelopes overstate freedom because integrating I preserves cross-redshift correlations — is well argued. Honest caveats: I_> bounds are model-dependent (not nonparametric); flat FLRW, smoothness, and the distance-duality relation are assumed. The explicit surviving loophole is new physics at z ≪ 0.01, below SNeIa reach.

Citation radar

This week’s radar splits cleanly between two currents. Three entries sit in gravitational-wave cosmology — phase-transition predictions, cosmological-collider loop signatures, and induced GWs from domain walls — reflecting a community still mining the early universe for signals across NANOGrav-to-LISA frequency bands. The other two are Feynman-integral technology: evaluating iterated integrals and solving canonical differential equations numerically. All five are young (a few weeks to two months) and each sits at ~5 citations, so these are early-momentum picks rather than established benchmarks. Where full text is unavailable I flag the guesswork.

arXiv:2605.15259 — TransitionListener v2.0: Robust gravitational wave predictions for cosmological phase transitions (Jonas Matuszak et al.)

No rendering was available, so this reads from title and metadata alone. The name signals a public code release: a “v2.0” update to a tool that maps particle-physics models of first-order phase transitions onto predicted stochastic GW spectra, with “robust” suggesting improved treatment of the notoriously uncertain transition parameters (nucleation rate, bubble-wall dynamics) that plague these forecasts. ~5 citations since mid-May. If the accumulation reflects anything, it is the standard pattern for phenomenology tooling: a maintained, ready-to-run pipeline gets cited by every follow-up model study that needs GW predictions without rebuilding the machinery. I cannot confirm the headline improvements from the text provided.

arXiv:2606.02744 — IterInt: Evaluating iterated integrals via differential equations (Gideon Baur et al.)

Text unavailable; I rely on the title plus a corroborating external reference. Notably, this paper is cited within Czakon–Tancredi (arXiv:2606.30354) below, which describes it as “a package that transforms iterated integrals into a differential-equation system and solves it numerically,” with the actual integration performed in C++ under a Mathematica interface. That framing — iterated integrals as the formal solutions of canonical differential equations — places IterInt squarely in the current push to make ε-factorized systems numerically tractable. ~5 citations since early June. The likely driver is the same one animating the whole subfield right now: a concrete, usable tool for evaluating the transcendental functions that appear beyond the polylogarithmic case, arriving just as multi-loop practitioners need exactly that.

arXiv:2605.21419 — Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-Handed Neutrino Loop (Jingtao You et al.)

No rendering available. The title places this in the cosmological-collider program, where heavy particles active during inflation imprint oscillatory, mass-dependent features in the primordial non-Gaussianity of curvature perturbations. The novelty signaled is a loop-level computation: right-handed neutrinos contributing at one loop rather than tree level, which is the natural way to probe fermions whose masses might otherwise leave no signal. This connects the collider formalism to leptogenesis-relevant physics, plausibly explaining early interest — it ties a fashionable inflationary observable to the seesaw sector. ~5 citations since May. Without the text I cannot verify the specific amplitude or the predicted signal strength.

arXiv:2604.25726 — Imprint of domain wall annihilation on induced gravitational waves (Rishav Roshan)

Roshan studies a minimal Z₂-symmetric real-scalar extension of the SM in which domain walls, made unstable by a small bias term, annihilate and dump most of their energy into the long-lived scalar. If that scalar dominates before decaying, it drives an early matter-dominated era that dramatically amplifies scalar-induced GWs (working in the non-linear regime via the Fernandez et al. simulation framework), while its eventual decay injects entropy that dilutes the direct domain-wall signal. The headline result is a distinctive double-peaked spectrum — a higher-frequency peak from wall annihilation, a lower-frequency peak from enhanced induced GWs — with both peaks potentially visible to THEIA and μARES, so detection in one band predicts the other.

The paper’s appeal is the correlated multi-band signature from a single symmetry-breaking event, a cleaner falsifiable target than isolated-source studies. ~5 citations in roughly two months, likely from the active domain-wall/induced-GW community (many self-citations to King, Borah, and collaborators are visible), reflecting momentum rather than settled impact.

arXiv:2606.30354 — Solution of Canonical Differential Equations for Integrals on Arbitrary Geometries (Michał Czakon et al.)

Czakon and Tancredi tackle a real bottleneck: canonical ε-factorized systems beyond the polylogarithmic case have connection matrices containing transcendental functions — elliptic or Calabi-Yau periods — for which closed forms are often unavailable, blocking numerical evaluation. Their key observation is that these functions are not arbitrary: since the original master integrals obey rational differential equations, so do the transcendental building blocks. Adjoining these auxiliary equations yields an enlarged purely-rational system solvable by standard numerical ODE methods, with correct analytic continuation guaranteed automatically. They demonstrate on the 220 two-loop masters for di-jet and γ+jet production through a heavy-quark loop — 16 square roots plus elliptic periods — and ship a lightweight, commercial-software-free C++ package built on Boost’s Bulirsch-Stoer solver, achieving sub-second double-precision evaluations.

~5 citations since late June. The draw is a general, deployable recipe that sidesteps the hardest obstacle to using canonical bases in realistic amplitudes: no special-function implementation needed, universally applicable to any Feynman integral. Given the surge of parallel efforts (Baur–Duhr, Liu–Zhang) it references, this lands in a hot and crowded space, positioned as the production-oriented option.

item.title: Thursday, July 23, 2026
item.description:
Spin polarization, Beijing and CERN

Two experiments made the day, both by measuring polarization in channels that were hard to reach. ATLAS reports 4.0σ evidence for a longitudinally polarized Z in electroweak W^±Zjj production (arXiv:2607.20246) — the direct sequel to last week’s doubly-longitudinal ZZ observation, pushing polarization fractions into the VBS-adjacent sector. At the other end of the mass scale, BESIII debuts a genuinely new trick: using secondary scattering off spectrometer material to measure final-state nucleon polarization, and turning it into the first determination of the relative phase between the proton’s psionic form factors (arXiv:2607.19948). Around these, a UHE-neutrino tension paper hardens the ANITA/KM3NeT/IceCube puzzle, and the neutrino-systematics thread the memory has tracked resurfaces on the energy-reconstruction side.

Themes

Polarization and EM measurements at colliders

The ATLAS WZjj result arXiv:2607.20246 (f_X0=0.32±0.09, SM-consistent) extends the electroweak-symmetry-breaking polarization program that produced the ZZ milestone on July 15 — the doubly-longitudinal fraction is still only bounded (<0.12). CMS delivers the most precise LHC measurement of γγ→ττ in ultraperipheral PbPb and tightens a_τ to [-0.039, 0.032] (arXiv:2607.20148).
