Koranga et al. arXiv:2607.10417 show that approximating Earth’s density with a single path-averaged value (rather than spatially resolved PREM) fabricates a degeneracy in (δ_CP,Δ_CPT,θ_CPT) that, at L≳5000 km, becomes indistinguishable from genuine BSM physics — a DUNE-like exposure could report a spurious ±3σ CPT violation. It’s the same lesson the week of degeneracy papers kept teaching, now aimed at the matter profile itself. On the input-precision side, T2K delivers its first double-differential kinematic-imbalance cross sections simultaneously on carbon and oxygen arXiv:2607.10638, arXiv:2607.10644, finding that no current generator describes the data across phase space — essential common systematics work for Hyper-K. And two double-beta papers land: ab-initio ⁴⁸Ca NMEs from VS-IMSRG showing the enlarged d_3/2pf space matters arXiv:2607.11733, and DarkSide-50’s first ³⁶Ar 2ν2EC limit arXiv:2607.11476.

Hadron spectroscopy: new states, sharper tools

A dense, experiment-anchored cluster. LHCb arXiv:2607.10595 performs an amplitude analysis of B⁻→Λ_c⁺p̅π⁻ and observes two new states, Σ_c(2900)⁰ and Σ_c(3200)⁰ — a real expansion of the charm-baryon landscape. BESIII arXiv:2607.11416 observes η_c→pp̅η for the first time at >10σ, carefully handling the interference solutions. On the theory/tooling side, Zhang et al. propose an improved moment QCD sum rule that eliminates the subjective OPE-convergence criteria arXiv:2607.11536, while two Regge-trajectory studies — quadruply-heavy pentaquarks arXiv:2607.10631 and a statistical model-selection analysis of light mesons arXiv:2607.11583 — probe the universality of level orderings. Femtoscopy continues as the interaction probe of choice, now for deuteron-hyperon systems arXiv:2607.10722 and a Coulomb-consistent K̅Ω treatment arXiv:2607.11321, extending the correlation-function wave the memory has followed.

Precision at present and future colliders

The precision-EW machinery keeps building. Fischer et al. update the Gfitter global fit with the new W-mass world average, extending it to the κ framework to bound the Higgs total width to ~10% without direct invisible searches, plus SMEFT projections for FCC-ee arXiv:2607.09861. Bar-Shalom et al. show FCC-ee can probe flavor-changing top interactions to Λ∼10 TeV — 40× the collision energy — simply by counting b-jets arXiv:2607.09856. On the fixed-order front, Gehrmann-De Ridder et al. complete the non-diagonal NNLO antenna-subtraction channels for heavy-quark pair production arXiv:2607.11741, and Dimitrakopoulos et al. bring MiNLO to full off-shell tt̅W arXiv:2607.11652.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.10606 — A high-precision lattice neutron EDM with a clever single-time-slice topological-charge trick and a non-Hermitian GEVP to kill excited states; the number to cite.
  • arXiv:2607.10272 — Williams argues the strong CP problem is contingent on optional global topology, not required by any known observable — a genuine foundational provocation.
  • arXiv:2607.10595 — LHCb observes two new Σ_c states; clean amplitude analysis, expands charm-baryon spectroscopy.
  • arXiv:2607.10417 — Earth’s matter profile itself can fake a 3σ CPT signal at DUNE-scale baselines; the degeneracy story reaches the geophysics.
  • arXiv:2607.09845 — A creative proposal to find heavy charged relics accumulated in terrestrial matter, with a liter-of-water pathfinder already probing new parameter space.

From the community

One field-facing piece: Grosso et al.’s VERaiPHY review arXiv:2607.10039 on verification and evaluation of increasingly autonomous ML systems before they underpin discovery claims — the natural sequel to last week’s LLM-auditing and AI-governance concerns, arguing that inductive bias is unavoidable and physicists’ judgment must encode the rigor.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.10760 The KM3NeT 220 PeV event: a neutrino messenger from the grand unification scale? — Barger (hep-ph) — reads the anomalous event as X→νν̅ decay of a 4.4×10⁸ GeV relic, with the mediator landing near 10¹⁶ GeV.
  • arXiv:2607.09808 ACT stands for Awkward Cosmology Theories — Del Grosso et al. (hep-ph) — a pointed critique showing that saving Starobinsky inflation from ACT data demands UV-unmotivated ingredients.
  • arXiv:2607.11139 Antineutron reconstruction in electromagnetic calorimeters with mixed-representation learning — Li et al. (hep-ex) — first direct momentum-magnitude measurement of antineutrons from ECAL alone, ~17% at 1 GeV/c.
  • arXiv:2607.11845 A Standard Model analysis of D⁰→ππ, KK, K_SK_S — Fleischer et al. (hep-ph) — predicts per-mille direct CP asymmetry in D⁰→K_SK_S, motivating precision measurement.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.10606 — The Neutron Electric Dipole Moment from Lattice QCD using a Background Electric Field (Thomas Blum et al.)

Blum et al. extract the θ̄-induced neutron EDM from the energy shift of a neutron in a static, imaginary-valued Euclidean electric field, arriving at d_n = -0.0050(4)_stat(8)_sys θ̅ efm at the physical point. Two methodological moves drive the precision. First, motivated by Feynman-Hellmann, they sample the topological charge density on a single time slice rather than integrating the global charge Qtop — the disonnected topological correlator is the noise bottleneck, and localizing it plus a full-volume low-mode average sharpens the signal dramatically. Second, because the background field deforms the nucleon and mixes parity, the naive positive-parity projector suffers large excited-state contamination; they instead solve a non-Hermitian (PT-symmetric, S-pseudo-Hermitian) GEVP in the space of the nucleon, its parity partner and excitations to isolate the true ground state. Reassuringly, EDM values agree across chiral-covariant and non-covariant interpolators and across gluonic vs. pseudoscalar-density definitions of the topological charge, and the global-charge method gives results consistent with (but far noisier than) the new estimator.

This is the kind of controlled number the EDM and 0νββ programs need to convert experimental limits into bounds on θ̅ and BSM CP-violating operators, and the local-charge + GEVP toolkit extends naturally to the Weinberg and chromo-EDM operators. Caveats are stated frankly: the calculation uses a single lattice spacing (a≈0.11 fm) and pion masses of 340–576 MeV, so discretization, finite-volume and chiral-extrapolation systematics are deferred to future work; the electro-quenched approximation is assumed benign (~1% for magnetic moments). It also lands amid ongoing dispute over whether the θ-term generates a nonzero nEDM at all.

arXiv:2607.10272 — On the Origins of the Strong CP Problem (Anthony G. Williams)

Williams argues that the strong CP problem is contingent, not mandatory. He defines “minimal QCD” — the standard Lagrangian plus local gauge invariance, causal locality, and the functional integral — and shows that essentially every established nonperturbative result attributed to topology follows within it without assuming the gauge-field configuration space decomposes into integer-valued sectors. The topological susceptibility emerges as χ=⟨Q̂²⟩/V=∂²ε_0/∂θ² with θ treated purely as a source parameter for the local operator q(x); the axial anomaly identifies the invariant θ̅=θ+M; and the ’t Hooft vertex, Witten–Veneziano (m_η’²⁼²N_fχ_YM/f_0²) and Leutwyler–Smilga (χ=Σ/∑_f m_f⁻¹) relations all rely only on local operators, semiclassical saddle points, or the large-N_c expansion. The integer-valued Q∈ℤ, the 2π-periodicity, the sector weighting e^iθQ, the physical θ-vacuum and hence the fine-tuning problem appear only after supplementing minimal QCD with smoothness/boundary assumptions (π_3(SU(3))=ℤ) — assumptions, he stresses, that typical distributional (non-differentiable) functional-integral configurations need not satisfy, and that lattice topology recovers only via added constructions (gradient flow, index theorem).

If this framing holds, the “problem” becomes a question about which additional structure Nature actually requires, reframing the recent Nelson-Barr/PQ solution flurry as answers to a possibly-optional question. The honest caveat is baked in: this is a foundational/logical clarification, not a new prediction. Williams explicitly does not claim a θ-term is forbidden by symmetry, does not dispute the θ↔pseudoscalar-mass equivalence, and concedes future theory or data could yet demand the global structure — in which case the entire conventional literature immediately reapplies.

arXiv:2607.10595 — Observation of new excited Σ_c⁰ states in B⁻→Λ_c⁺p̅π⁻ (LHCb collaboration et al.)

An LHCb amplitude analysis of B⁻→Λ_c⁺p̅π⁻ using the full 9 fb⁻¹ Run 1+2 dataset (37.0×10³ signal decays, 5.1% combinatorial background) resolves the Λ_c⁺π⁻ spectrum into the known Σ_c(2455)⁰, Σ_c(2520)⁰ and Σ_c(2800)⁰ plus two new states, Σ_c(2900)⁰ and Σ_c(3200)⁰ — the first new excited Σ_c⁰ baryons in over two decades. The two-resonance description of the ~2.8 GeV region (splitting the old BaBar Σ_c(2800)⁰ into overlapping states) is favored at 7.5σ, and the Σ_c(3200)⁰ is observed at 12.0σ. Combining the two solution families, they measure m_Σ_c(3200)⁰⁼³.186±0.006±0.015 GeV/c², Γ=0.133±0.018±0.046 GeV. The Σ_c(2520)⁰ spin-parity is pinned to 3/2⁺ (>6σ) and the Σ_c(2455)⁰ spin to 1/2. Candidate interpretations span 2S/1P for the Σ_c(2900)⁰ and 2P/3S for the Σ_c(3200)⁰.

This materially expands the sparse Σ_c sector — only three states were previously established — providing masses and widths to confront the crowded quark-model predictions for 2S/1D/2P λ- and ρ-mode excitations, part of today’s experiment-anchored spectroscopy cluster. The central honest caveat is that spin-parity cannot be unambiguously fixed: multiple J^P assignments give nearly degenerate likelihoods, yielding two solution groups (A and B) statistically indistinguishable (2Δlnℒ<1) yet giving very different masses, widths and fit fractions for the Σ_c(2800)⁰/Σ_c(2900)⁰ pair — group A matches Belle’s Σ_c(2800)⁰ (which sees no Σ_c(2900)⁰), group B does not. Only the Σ_c(3200)⁰ parameters are robust across solutions.

(The digest’s two other “worth a look” picks — arXiv:2607.10417 and arXiv:2607.09845 — were not included in today’s full-text batch, so no deep dive is possible here.)

item.title: Monday, July 13, 2026
item.description:
The vibe today

After a fortnight of tool-building and precision-machinery papers, today reads like the phenomenologists reclaiming the floor. It’s a broad, model-builder’s-and-spectroscopist’s day — no single collaboration bombshell, but a wide field of theory: mass matrices and majorons, reheating histories, a dozen exotic hadrons, and neutrinos pressed into service as probes of everything from the neutron-star equation of state to the Earth’s deep interior. The through-line is neutrinos as instruments. They turn up as terrestrial gauges of in-medium hyperon potentials, as scanners of the planet’s density profile, and as messengers filtered through the dark-matter spikes around active galactic nuclei. The community is increasingly comfortable treating the neutrino not as the object of study but as the flashlight.

The other half of the room is doing hadron spectroscopy and dark-sector model-building, both in a consolidating mood. Exotic states — molecular, compact, tetra- and pentaquark — get computed across half a dozen frameworks, while the dark sector keeps its now-habitual reliance on discrete symmetries and non-standard reheating to fix relic abundances. And two threads the memory has been tracking resurface cleanly: the b→sℓℓ long-distance-versus-C_9 debate gets a fresh data-driven entry, and the Belle II GNN calorimeter trigger — whose radiation-reliability was stress-tested back on July 3 — is now reported fully commissioned and running at low latency.

A cerebral, diffuse day, then: lots of frameworks, several genuinely useful reinterpretations, and one nice instance of a bound being quietly deflated.

Themes

Neutrinos as terrestrial probes

The day’s most distinctive cluster is a trilogy by Nowak (arXiv:2607.09255, arXiv:2607.09273, arXiv:2607.09280) arguing that charged-current accelerator-neutrino interactions on argon produce Λ and Σ hyperons inside the nucleus, turning hyperon final-state interactions at SBND and DUNE into a laboratory handle on the in-medium potentials that govern the neutron-star “hyperon puzzle.” The forecasts are sobering but honest: a naive Fisher analysis promises sub-MeV precision on U_Λ, but marginalizing over the low-density slope degrades that to several MeV, and YN cross-section systematics dominate U_Σ. The third paper links this all the way to quarkyonic hyperon onset and the maximum mass. Alongside, Zhuridov et al. (arXiv:2607.09591) push neutrino oscillation tomography of the Earth to second-order perturbation theory with a multi-shell scheme that handles density jumps between layers — again casting GeV atmospheric neutrinos at KM3NeT/DUNE/Hyper-K as geophysical instruments.

AGN neutrino–dark matter scattering

A small but pointed exchange. Abbaslu et al. (arXiv:2607.08833) build a model in which high-energy AGN neutrinos scatter off the dark-matter spike around supermassive black holes, distorting the flavor ratio that IceCube-Gen2 will soon measure precisely. On the very same day, Farzan (arXiv:2607.08904) revisits the flux-attenuation bounds derived from exactly this physics and shows they are far more model-dependent than advertised: for a light vector mediator well below the collision energy, the neutrino energy loss — and hence the attenuation — becomes negligible, relaxing the limits substantially. It’s a healthy reminder that “spike constraints” on neutrino-DM scattering carry hidden microphysics assumptions.

Dark relics from discrete symmetries and reheating

The memory’s running theme — discrete symmetries doing double duty and reheating histories setting abundances — is well represented. Fujisawa et al. (arXiv:2607.09131) build minimal majoron dark matter from an exact Z_N⊂U(1)_B-L gauge symmetry, with Planck-suppressed operators generating the mass; Z_5 is excluded by neutrino decays but Z_7 predicts a 1–10 MeV majoron probeable by COSI. Fernández Navarro (arXiv:2607.08814) identifies a “minimal high-quality QCD axion” as a 5D Wilson-line phase with exponential quality protection and no bulk QCD. On the reheating side, Mambrini’s “seesaw reheating” (arXiv:2607.08828) ties the reheating temperature to lepton-number breaking and sterile-neutrino dark matter, while Barman et al. (arXiv:2607.09282) study leptogenesis with sub-sphaleron reheating temperatures — a direct sequel to yesterday’s low-reheating leptogenesis result. Borah et al.’s “Dark Phoenix” (arXiv:2607.08838) is the most inventive: dark matter that thermally overproduces is rescued by a transient post-freeze-out decay window opened by finite-temperature mass effects and shut by a first-order phase transition.

Hadron spectroscopy and exotics

A dense, methodologically varied cluster. Assi et al. (arXiv:2607.08817) deploy renormalon-subtracted pNRQCD with GFMC to predict triply- and fully-heavy baryon masses, undershooting lattice by 125–175 MeV in a controlled 1/m_Q pattern. QCD sum rules deliver a fully-beauty tensor tetraquark at 18.5 GeV (Agaev et al. arXiv:2607.09354) and ssscc̅ pentaquark candidates in the J/ψΩ spectrum (Wang arXiv:2607.09430). Gordillo et al. (arXiv:2607.09288) run diffusion Monte Carlo on light hexaquarks, finding no deeply bound compact six-quark states but a deuteron-like molecular configuration. And Wang et al. (arXiv:2607.09093) use ψ(4660) decays as a molecular-nature test for the Z_c/Z_cs states via triangle loops — continuing the week’s molecular-picture consolidation.

Precision QCD/EW and threshold effects

Timely and concrete. Nason et al. (arXiv:2607.09539) present three NLO+PS generators incorporating threshold-enhanced non-relativistic effects in tt̅ production — directly aimed at the recently observed near-threshold enhancement (pseudoscalar/”toponium”) channel at ATLAS and CMS. Biello et al. (arXiv:2607.09124) push mixed QCD×EW corrections to charged-current Drell-Yan at high transverse mass, in the same precision-DY lineage as last week’s resonance-aware MC@NLO work. Weißwange (arXiv:2607.08847) reports the complete one-loop SM renormalization in the BMHV non-anticommuting-γ_5 scheme with symmetry-restoring counterterms, and Kovner et al. (arXiv:2607.09337) fold running-coupling effects into anti-collinear BFKL resummation.

Flavor windows in B decays

Bordone et al. (arXiv:2607.09458) give an updated data-driven dispersive analysis of B→K^*μ⁺μ⁻ using LHCb’s full angular distribution, finding C_9 below its SM value but significantly closer once long-distance contributions are constrained by data — tension no more than 2σ. This is the natural continuation of Ciuchini et al.’s July 3 argument that hadronic effects, not a short-distance shift, drive the anomalies. Complementing it, Colangelo et al. (arXiv:2607.09216) fit Belle II b→u data in a SMEFT-consistent generalized Hamiltonian, and Zhang et al. (arXiv:2607.09573) deliver the first NLO SCET sum-rule form factors for B→D_1(2420)/D_1’(2430).

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.08904 — Farzan deflates AGN-spike neutrino-DM bounds by showing they hinge on mediator mass; a clean cautionary result, doubly striking landing the same day as a paper deriving flavor signals from the same physics.
  • arXiv:2607.09273 — The meat of the Nowak trilogy: neutrino-induced hyperon FSI as a terrestrial probe of the neutron-star EoS, with honest degradation of the forecast once systematics are marginalized.
  • arXiv:2607.09539 — NLO+PS generators for threshold-enhanced tt̅, directly relevant to the recent toponium-like observation at the LHC.
  • arXiv:2607.09458 — A data-driven dispersive reading of B→K^*μμ that pulls C_9 back toward the SM; the latest word in the long-distance-vs-new-physics debate.
  • arXiv:2607.09347 — The Belle II GNN calorimeter trigger, fault-tested here on July 3, now commissioned and running at 1.05 µs latency with bit-accurate validation — the ML-trigger wave reaching production.

From the community

The ALEGRO 2026 workshop report (arXiv:2607.09457) surveys advanced wakefield accelerators and the ongoing 10 TeV linear-collider design study launched after the US P5 recommendations. It’s a useful map of where the plasma/structure-wakefield community stands as the European Strategy update looms — the long-horizon collider question that has shadowed the week’s facility-timeline anxieties.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.08816 High Energy Photon Polarimetry at Lepton Colliders — de Lima et al. (hep-ph) — converted photons at Belle II as a route to Bell-inequality and quantum-discord measurements with GeV-scale diphotons.
  • arXiv:2607.09621 Search for soft unclustered energy patterns — CMS Collaboration (hep-ex) — data-scouting SUEP search setting the most stringent limits yet on heavy scalar mediators in strongly-coupled hidden valleys.
  • arXiv:2607.09352 Constraints on Sub-MeV Dark Matter from Solar Reflection with DAMIC-M — Aggarwal et al. (hep-ex) — world-competitive ultralight-mediator limits from just ~1.3 kg-day of skipper-CCD data.
  • arXiv:2607.09531 Perusing confining pseudoreal theories — Cacciapaglia et al. (hep-th) — a comprehensive classification predicting emergent massless spin-1 states, testable on the lattice.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.08904 — Revisiting bounds on neutrino dark matter interaction at spikes (Yasaman Farzan)

The finding: The much-quoted “spike” bounds on neutrino–DM scattering — derived from the attenuation of AGN neutrino fluxes traversing the dense DM cusp around supermassive black holes — collapse for light vector mediators. Farzan’s point is kinematic: the cascade equation contains both a loss term (-σΦ) and a regeneration term (the down-scattered flux re-populating each energy bin). Previous analyses (Cline et al., Cline–Puel, Dixit–Mohlabeng–Razzaque) kept only the loss term, valid only if each collision removes a neutrino from the beam. But when m_Z’²/(2m_DM)≪E_ν, the differential cross section is sharply peaked at E’_ν≃E_ν — scattering is nearly forward, energy loss negligible, and the two terms cancel. Defining an effective suppression factor f, for Φ∝E_ν⁻³.2 and m_Z’²/m_DM=2 GeV, Farzan finds 2×10⁻³<f<10⁻² across the 1.5–15 TeV NGC 1068 window — relaxing the “most stringent” bound by up to ~1000×.

Why it matters: Landing the same day as Abbaslu et al.’s paper deriving AGN flavor signals from this same scattering, it’s a clean cautionary counterpoint: “spike constraints” on σ_νDM carry hidden microphysics (mediator mass, symmetric vs. asymmetric DM, flavor structure). Farzan further notes symmetric DM can annihilate to νν̅, and flavor-selective couplings can suppress attenuation while still distorting flavor ratios — leaving room for IceCube-Gen2/KM3NeT to discover spike effects rather than merely exclude them. Caveat: the companion analysis establishing the flavor phenomenology is “work in progress,” so the positive-signal claims rest partly on unpublished results.

arXiv:2607.09273 — Neutrino-induced hyperon final-state interactions as constraints on the in-medium hyperon potential (Jaroslaw Nowak)

What they did: Nowak proposes that charged-current accelerator (anti)neutrinos on ⁴⁰Ar create Λ,Σ hyperons inside the nucleus, so their final-state interactions become a terrestrial probe of the in-medium potentials U_Y(ρ) that drive the neutron-star “hyperon puzzle.” Using the internal StrangeMC generator, three observables respond monotonically to the potentials: the trapped-Λ fraction and escaping-Λ momentum (for U_Λ), the escaping-Σ momentum, and a kaon-vetoed FSI-Σ⁺ tag (a final state the weak vertex cannot make) for U_Σ. A detector-level Fisher forecast gives δU_Λ≈0.3 MeV and δU_Σ≈3–4 MeV at fixed low-density slope γ. Fed through a GM1 relativistic mean field anchored to established depths, the same potentials yield M_max=1.94 M_⊙ and Λ_1.4=1034.

The honesty: The headline sub-MeV number is heavily caveated. Because hyperons are born below saturation, U_Λ(ρ_0) and γ are 99.8% anti-correlated; marginalizing over γ (which the data alone fix only to δγ≈0.8) degrades δU_Λ to 5.6 MeV. Two further systematics — the transport prescription (−6 MeV) and YN cross sections (−5/+2 MeV) — push the realistic U_Λ budget to ~10 MeV. Worse, the YN uncertainty biases U_Σ by 𝒪(150) MeV, not an artifact of the Σ⁺ tag but because the Λ spectrum itself is YN-sensitive. The propagated M_max is explicitly an inference dominated by the external high-density prior, not a neutrino measurement; the ~0.3 M_⊙ EOS-model systematic dwarfs the statistical reach. StrangeMC is uncommissioned against community generators — a stated next step.

arXiv:2607.09539 — Top-Antitop Production and Decay at Threshold at the LHC in QCD Perturbation Theory (Paolo Nason et al.)

What they did: Nason, Pelliccioli, Re and Rottoli deliver three NLO+PS generators (thr1, thr2, bb4l) incorporating threshold-enhanced (Coulomb/Sommerfeld) corrections in tt̅ production, extending their earlier NRR work up to (α_s/v)⁶ and, crucially, with finite-width treatment (thr2 modifies the phase space for off-shell tops; bb4l uses the full b_bbar_4l off-shell code). In the “ATLAS bin” (m_tt̅<350 GeV, p^⋆<50 GeV) they find total cross sections near 10 pb with a threshold excess over baseline NLO of ~4 pb — compatible with the Garzelli et al. NRQCD result and with the 8.5–9.3 pb “η_t” numbers CMS/ATLAS extract. The perturbative series converges: truncating at α_s³ already captures the full result to better than 1 pb, so all-orders GFRW resummation is unnecessary at LHC resolution.

Why it matters: This directly addresses the recent near-threshold “toponium” observation, and sharpens the interpretation. The authors argue forcefully that (i) the pseudoscalar dominance follows from the Landau–Yang theorem for gluon fusion regardless of bound-state formation; (ii) toponium is part of the perturbative QCD cross section, so claiming an “excess above QCD consistent with QCD-predicted toponium” is contradictory; and (iii) the genuine bound-state contribution is small (~2.6–4.5 pb depending on generator/scale) and cannot be cleanly separated from continuum given the top width smearing. A new physical effect: imposing double-top virtuality cuts suppresses the sub-threshold cross section via phase-space reduction, cutting the bound-state yield by ~1 pb — captured by thr2/bb4l but not thr1. Caveat: the exact finite-width resummation formula (Appendix A) is derived but not implemented; single-top contamination near threshold requires a full experimental signal/background study the authors defer.

item.title: Thursday, July 9, 2026
item.description:
The vibe today

After a week spent rebuilding tools from first principles and confronting the sticker-shock of next-generation facilities, today feels like the field cashing in on that infrastructure investment. Two of the papers that the week’s syntheses flagged as landmarks — the pixel-level confirmation of the Fermi-LAT 20 GeV halo excess (arXiv:2607.08552) and the direct-neutron-readout hadronic calorimeter (arXiv:2607.08587) — actually post today, and they arrive alongside a fresh crop of software releases, a quantum-computing review, and the transformer-based cell-level calorimeter work that has been the throughline of the week’s ML story. It is a builder’s day.

The intellectual center of gravity, though, is neutrinos — specifically the Dirac-versus-Majorana question, attacked from four directions at once. A null half-life limit from AMoRE, a cosmological ΔN_eff handle on Dirac right-handed neutrinos, a machine-learning-assisted revisit of mass textures, and an unusually abstract algebraic reformulation of particle–antiparticle coherence all converge on the same fundamental ambiguity. Nobody resolved it today, but the sheer variety of angles — nuclear, cosmological, phenomenological, group-theoretic — is a good snapshot of how central this one question remains.

The rest of the day is healthily diffuse: hadron structure and heavy-ion phenomenology, a couple of LISA methodology papers tightening how we report sensitivity, and the usual quiet stream of formal hep-th. No single blockbuster, but a satisfying breadth.

Themes

The Majorana question, from four directions

The AMoRE Collaboration reports the first dedicated search for neutrinoless double electron capture in ⁴⁰Ca using their ⁴⁰Ca¹⁰⁰MoO_4 cryogenic detectors, setting T⁰ν_1/2 > 1.7×10²² yr (arXiv:2607.08039) — a nice demonstration that a 0νββ-optimized crystal can be repurposed for a complementary LNV channel. From cosmology, Liu et al. (arXiv:2607.08082) point out that if the right-handed neutrinos in a Z’-portal dark matter model are Dirac rather than Majorana, they contribute to ΔN_eff, giving upcoming CMB measurements a distinct lever on the neutrino nature that reshapes the entire detectability landscape. Kitagawa et al. (arXiv:2607.08384) revisit one- and two-zero mass textures under the latest oscillation and cosmological bounds, using flow matching to map the surviving structures and their δ_CP predictions — the CMB+BAO mass-sum cut does most of the killing. And on the formal end, Romero (arXiv:2607.08739) reorganizes the four-dimensional particle/antiparticle–helicity space of a massive neutrino into an internal SU(2) pseudospin, recasting the Majorana condition as a projection and classifying pseudo-Dirac splittings and 0νββ mass factors algebraically. Four papers, one question — a fair reflection of where the field’s anxiety lives as JUNO, DUNE, and Hyper-K approach.

Tooling up: software, ML, and quantum

The week’s “rebuild the tools” mood carries straight into today. AMFlow 2.0 (arXiv:2607.08477) brings a new recursion mode, a faster differential-equation solver, and support for modern IBP reducers, benchmarked on a three-loop five-point topology — squarely in the auxiliary-mass-flow ecosystem that keeps multi-loop numerics tractable. On the event-generation side, Doherty et al. (arXiv:2607.08723) attack the perennial negative-weight problem with optimal-transport metrics (Energy Mover’s Distance and a spectral variant) for cell resampling, reducing bias relative to existing techniques — a direct heir to the week’s “Watts per event” sustainability thread. Rodrigo’s overview of quantum computing in QCD (arXiv:2607.08169) surveys the same territory soberly, cataloguing where quantum algorithms might help and where NISQ hardware still can’t. And the transformer-based collimated-photon identifier from low-level calorimeter cells (arXiv:2607.08175) is exactly the calorimetry chapter of the week’s flavor-tagging-to-raw-reconstruction ML arc: cell-level beats shower-shape variables decisively, and the transformer even does direct invariant-mass regression to suppress π⁰/η fakes.

Dark matter’s velocity puzzle, and a new gravitational window

The 20 GeV Galactic halo excess gets its independent stress-test today: Stenhouse et al. (arXiv:2607.08552) reproduce the cell-aggregated Fermi-LAT result and extend it to a pixel-level likelihood with PSF forward-folding, confirming the spectrum and its ∼0.55–0.72 TeV WIMP best fit. The honest punchline is that only low-velocity-enhanced (resonant Sommerfeld or Breit-Wigner) annihilation survives the joint dwarf-limit, present-day-rate, and relic-density constraints — and even that requires a resonance fine-tuned to the halo velocity. This is precisely the open question the weekly memory posed, now sharpened. Meanwhile Gan et al. (arXiv:2607.08248) show LISA can probe quadratically coupled ultralight dark matter at two characteristic frequencies and, crucially, without the screening that hobbles terrestrial searches — a genuinely new detection window rather than a reinterpretation.

Detectors and flux inputs for the intensity frontier

Two papers quietly do the unglamorous work the next decade depends on. The Pb/Gd-loaded-scintillator calorimeter (arXiv:2607.08587) reads out delayed neutron-capture energy to recover invisible hadronic energy, improving prompt resolution from 21.8% to 13.3% with no event rejection — a hardware answer to hadronic fluctuations. And Cheng et al. (arXiv:2607.08310) deliver a precision 3D atmospheric-neutrino flux built on the Honda framework, incorporating in-Earth muon propagation for the first time and reducing hadronic systematics across seven detector sites — essential common input for JUNO, Hyper-K, DUNE, ORCA, and the direct-detection neutrino fog.

Hadron structure and heavy-ion

A steady undercurrent: Wu et al. (arXiv:2607.08040) use a complex-momentum-representation-plus-Green’s-function scheme to describe X(3872), T_cc⁺, and Z_c(3900) as bound states and G(3900) as a P-wave resonance in one unified DD^* framework — continuing the week’s molecular-picture consolidation. Jana et al. (arXiv:2607.08457) propose eP/eA GTMD ratios for spin and orbital angular momentum at the EIC, and Li et al. (arXiv:2607.08669) extract pion nuclear fragmentation functions with explicit A and ν dependence. On the theory-cleanup side, Hoyos (arXiv:2607.08569) resolves the pseudo-gauge ambiguity in spin polarization by reframing it as spurious symmetries with vanishing total charge.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.08552 — Independent pixel-level confirmation of the 20 GeV halo excess; the velocity-structure argument narrows viable WIMP models to fine-tuned resonant annihilation.
  • arXiv:2607.08587 — A hardware fix for the invisible-hadronic-energy problem: direct neutron readout cuts calorimeter resolution by nearly half without discarding events.
  • arXiv:2607.08175 — Transformer on raw calorimeter cells for collimated diphotons, with direct mass regression — the calorimetry front of the week’s ML-reconstruction wave.
  • arXiv:2607.08663 — Leptogenesis works for arbitrarily low reheating temperatures with k≥4 inflaton potentials, and the final asymmetry is strikingly insensitive to the RHN mass and reheating temperature.
  • arXiv:2607.08039 — AMoRE turns a 0νββ crystal into a competitive 0ν2EC probe, broadening the lepton-number-violation search program.

From the community

Bhattacharya’s proceeding on early-career issues (arXiv:2607.08131) is the human counterpart to the week’s recurring theme of decades-long facility timelines: it surveys the future-collider landscape from an ECR viewpoint, reports large-scale survey feedback, and takes a clear-eyed look at the job market, outreach, and the double-edged role of AI. Worth reading precisely because the machines being debated now will define these careers to 2060.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.08445 — A corrected, arbitrary-strength expression for LISA’s stochastic-background SNR, showing the commonly quoted values are inaccurate and that SNR contours are bounded from above; data on Zenodo.
  • arXiv:2607.08629 — González-Jiménez’s detailed lecture notes on relativistic quasielastic lepton-nucleus scattering — a useful entry point for students heading into neutrino-nucleus interactions.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.08552 — The 20 GeV Galactic Halo Excess: Pixel-Level Confirmation and Consistency with Sub-TeV WIMP Annihilation (Trinity Rosebud Stenhouse et al.)

Stenhouse, Ghag & Deppisch independently reproduce Totani’s cell-aggregated Fermi-LAT halo excess and extend it to a pixel-level Poisson likelihood on native 0.125° maps with energy-dependent PSF forward-folding and bright-source masking. The two methods agree on the spectrum — a peak at ~20.8 GeV — with the pixel-level normalization ~20% higher for the ρ² halo, confirming the feature is not an artifact of 10° binning. The excess is centrally concentrated (angular profile χ²/ν≃5–7 for NFW vs 30 for isotropic), spectrally and spatially distinct from the few-GeV GCE, and stable under a foreground-systematics suite and an injection-null test (a distorted-ICS mock with no halo yields ≤10% of the observed peak). Prompt s-wave fits give mχ≃0.55 TeV (W⁺W⁻) and 0.72 TeV (bb̄) with ⟨σv⟩≃1×10⁻²⁴ cm³ s⁻¹.

Why it matters: this is exactly the independent stress-test the weekly memory flagged. The headline tension is with dwarf-spheroidal limits, ℛ≃5.1 face-value, widening to 1.6–9.3 once foreground choice (GALPROP vs GIEM dominates, halving the flux) and J-factor uncertainties are folded in — so s-wave is not excluded but not comfortable. Crucially, p/d-wave over-resolves the dwarf tension but misses relic abundance by ~7 orders of magnitude; decay is disfavored by the IGRB. Only resonant Sommerfeld/Breit-Wigner survives, supplying the needed ≈45× boost — but requiring a fine-tuned above-threshold resonance and a structured dark sector. Caveat honestly stated: χ²/ν∼8 from coherent diffuse residuals, and AMS-02 antiprotons independently disfavor direct bb̄; this is “consistency,” not detection.

arXiv:2607.08587 — A Novel Hadronic Calorimeter With A Direct Neutron Readout (I. Giomataris et al.)

Giomataris et al. simulate (Geant4, benchmarked against FLUKA) a sampling calorimeter of alternating Pb absorbers and Gd-loaded LAB scintillator that reads out both the prompt scintillation and a delayed signal from neutron moderation and capture. In a six-layer prototype (3.66 λ_I) hit by 10 GeV protons, ~197 neutrons/proton are captured with a median capture time of 11.1 μs; the delayed deposited energy is almost perfectly proportional to capture multiplicity (R²=0.9998, slope 7.97 MeV/neutron), giving direct calibration. Gadolinium’s key benefit is timing, not yield: 0.5% Gd collects >85% of captures within 20 μs versus ~10% for pure LAB. Because neutron production tracks the invisible hadronic energy, a branch-wise event-by-event correction using the delayed signal improves prompt resolution from 21.8% to 13.3% — a ~63% variance reduction — with no event rejection.

Why it matters: this is a hardware attack on the invisible-energy fluctuations that fundamentally limit hadronic resolution, complementary to dual-readout. The intrinsic neutron-counting resolution (~7%) is far below the 21.8% calorimetric resolution, confirming that neutron-production fluctuations, not the detector, dominate — and can be measured out. Events binned by fixed neutron multiplicity show resolution falling to ~6%, suggesting the method scales favorably to higher energies. Caveats are explicit: a single 10 GeV energy, a shallow preliminary geometry, and no optical-photon transport, photosensor, or electronics modeling yet — the 13.3% is a proof-of-principle, not a device spec.

arXiv:2607.08175 — Transformer-based machine learning using low-level calorimeter signals for collimated photon identification (Gabriel Matos et al.)

(Abstract only.) The authors use calorimeter cell-level information to separate highly collimated diphoton signatures — from light axion-like-particle decays — from isolated single photons, systematically comparing six architectures spanning high-level shower-shape approaches and direct cell-level methods. Cell-level ML decisively outperforms shower-shape variables, with a Transformer best overall and an MLP Mixer offering a resource-constrained option for trigger-level deployment. Beyond classification, the Transformer performs direct invariant-mass regression from cells, sharpening light-resonance characterization and adding a handle to suppress π⁰ and η fake-photon backgrounds.

Why it matters: this is the calorimetry front of the week’s ML-reconstruction arc — the same raw-input-beats-engineered-features lesson seen in flavor tagging, now applied to fine-grained EM showers. Direct mass regression from cells is the notable step beyond classification. No numerical performance figures are available in the provided text.

item.title: Wednesday, July 8, 2026
item.description:
The vibe today

A theory-heavy, model-builder’s day — the kind where the phenomenologists outnumber the collaborations and the whiteboard energy is all about structure: mass matrices, discrete symmetries, seesaws, and the stubborn puzzle of why the QCD vacuum angle is zero. After a week dominated by precision machinery and neutrino-oscillation stress tests, the field pivoted today toward the deep flavor questions that never really go away. There’s no single bombshell, but there is a clear intellectual center of gravity, and it sits at the intersection of flavor hierarchies, CP violation, and strong CP.

Two quieter continuities run underneath. The joint QCD+QED factorization program that the memory has been tracking for two weeks — lepton distribution functions, sub-percent precision beyond pure-QCD factorization — got its most ambitious application yet, and the proton-mass/gravitational-form-factor thread from earlier this week kept building. Meanwhile the dark sector stayed in its now-familiar diversifying mode: winos, dark neutrons, massive gravitons, multipolar freeze-out, and a genuinely eye-catching (if unconfirmed) dark-photon hint from a tabletop experiment.

And a couple of papers reached for the deep water: a first collider bound on Born-rule violations, and a pair of reflective reviews tracing how QCD and cosmology grew into precision sciences. A cerebral day, more about frameworks than discoveries.

Themes

Flavor, neutrinos, and the geometry of mixing

The densest cluster today is pure flavor model-building. Xing proposes a “neutrino cuboid” parametrization that accommodates tribimaximal mixing and near-degenerate normal-ordered masses in a cubic limit, offering a testable correlation for JUNO/DUNE/T2HK (arXiv:2607.07311). Hao et al. deliver the first comprehensive Δ(96) Modular Littlest Seesaw study, scanning 35 viable breaking patterns that go beyond the usual TM_1 paradigm (arXiv:2607.07865). Yang derives the CKM CP phase perturbatively from rephasing invariants of hierarchical mass matrices (arXiv:2607.06985), and Darricau et al. revisit cLFV asymmetries in scotogenic “T1-2-A” models (arXiv:2607.07484). Bonilla et al. tie neutrino mass to dark-matter stability in minimal S_3/D_4 three-Higgs-doublet models (arXiv:2607.07853). Also here, though a matter-physics paper: Chaulagain et al.’s algebraic dissection of three-flavor oscillations via Cayley–Hamilton and DMP resummation (arXiv:2607.07213), which was already flagged in the weekly memory as a degeneracy-breaking tool and separates genuine from fake CP in closed form.

Strong CP, from three directions at once

A striking coincidence: three quite different attacks on the strong CP problem land the same day. Baer et al. continue their storyline — the memory has tracked it all week — arguing that once the MSSM μ-term is forbidden by anomaly-free Z_n^R symmetry, an accidental Peccei-Quinn symmetry falls out and, via Kim-Nilles, “serendipitously” delivers a DFSZ axion that solves strong CP while regenerating μ (arXiv:2607.07921). Fileviez Perez et al. take the Nelson-Barr route: a universal seesaw with spontaneous CP violation keeps θ̅=0 at tree level while generating the CKM phase and the whole charged-fermion hierarchy (arXiv:2607.07794). And Figueroa et al. flip the sign of the question, using a dark-sector θ-term as a feature — sourcing dark-neutron self-interactions and CP-violating dark electric dipole moments visible in direct detection (arXiv:2607.07406). Strong CP as bug, as solved problem, and as dark-matter engine, all in one morning.

QCD+QED factorization goes inclusive

The lepton-distribution-function program the memory has been following reaches a milestone: Qiu et al. present the first calculation of single-inclusive hadron and jet production at large p_T in lepton-hadron scattering within joint QCD+QED factorization, with DGLAP kernels in both couplings and a strategy to extract nonperturbative LDFs at JLab and the EIC (arXiv:2607.07664). Its companion in spirit, Mantry et al., shows QED radiation gives order-one corrections to DIS cross sections but leaves longitudinal spin asymmetries robust at the few-percent level — the observable of choice for SMEFT extraction at SoLID/EIC (arXiv:2607.07811). Marzocca et al. push the parallel “joint fits” theme, showing PDF profiling degrades high-mass Drell-Yan SMEFT bounds in a strongly flavour-dependent way — worst for first-generation operators tied to high-x valence luminosities (arXiv:2607.07791), a direct sequel to the PDF-absorbs-new-physics warning from last week. Sterman’s review (arXiv:2607.07908) frames the whole enterprise historically.

The gluonic origin of mass

Meziani et al. lay out an experimental roadmap to the gluonic trace anomaly — the dominant source of the proton mass — reconstructing the scalar gluonic trace form factor from DVCS, near-threshold quarkonium production, and the sigma-term, with consistency checks against lattice and the instanton-liquid model (arXiv:2607.07969). Deng et al. complement this from theory, computing the pion’s A and D gravitational form factors in light-front holographic QCD (arXiv:2607.07305). Together they extend the gravitational-form-factor thread that ran through this week’s proton-structure papers.

Dark matter keeps diversifying

No WIMP renaissance, just a widening search. Frolovsky et al. connect Starobinsky supergravity to the MSSM and land on a 3 TeV thermal wino with a disappearing-track signature for a 100 TeV collider (arXiv:2607.07193); Bose et al. show an early matter-dominated epoch reopens excluded multipolar-DM parameter space (arXiv:2607.07956); Megias et al. offer massive-graviton DM from a gapped continuum (arXiv:2607.07295). On the experimental side, Belle II sets the world’s best ALP–photon limits over most of 0.17–5 GeV (arXiv:2607.07800), while PHELEX reports a possible diurnal dark-photon signal at 10–40 eV (arXiv:2607.07074) — intriguing, but explicitly awaiting independent confirmation.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.07664 — First inclusive-hadron/jet calculation in joint QCD+QED factorization; the LDF program’s most concrete deliverable yet, aimed squarely at the EIC.
  • arXiv:2607.07800 — Belle II’s world-leading ALP–photon limits, up to 9× better than prior results across a broad mass range.
  • arXiv:2607.07969 — A clean, measurable path to the trace-anomaly contribution to the proton mass, cross-checked against lattice.
  • arXiv:2607.07921 — Baer et al.’s “serendipitous” SUSY solution to strong CP; the through-line of the week’s cornered-WIMP-to-axion pivot.
  • arXiv:2607.06938 — A genuinely first-of-its-kind bound on Born-rule violations from PEP Bhabha data (ε<0.042); a foundational-quantum test wearing collider clothes.

From the community

Two reflective, pedagogical pieces rather than results. Sterman’s “QCD for electroweak precision measurements: Foundations” (arXiv:2607.07908) traces the historical sweep from QED-as-precision-theory through DIS to modern precision EW — a useful orientation for a field increasingly defined by joint frameworks. And Laine et al. offer a genuinely accessible tutorial on cosmological perturbations, complete with Python scripts (arXiv:2607.06983) — the kind of open, teachable resource that quietly lowers the barrier to entry.

Also noted

  • BESIII observes e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻ηJ/ψ at 6.0σ but finds no isoscalar X(3900) partner to the Z_c(3900) (arXiv:2607.07446).
  • Hagelstein et al. find their hadronic-VP contribution to muonic-hydrogen HFS differs from all prior evaluations by ~10× the anticipated CREMA/FAMU precision (arXiv:2607.07658).
  • First numerical-relativity simulations of subsolar-mass strange-star mergers, with f_2/f_cut cleanly separating them from neutron-star binaries (arXiv:2607.07668).
  • Two GRAPES-3 GNN pipelines — muon/hadron track separation and cosmic-ray energy reconstruction (arXiv:2607.07263, arXiv:2607.07265) — extending the graph-network wave into air-shower arrays.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.07664 — Single inclusive hadron and jet production in lepton-hadron scattering (Jian-Wei Qiu et al.)

The first calculation of high-p_T single-inclusive hadron (π^±,K^±) and jet production in e+h→H+X within joint QCD+QED collinear factorization, treating collision-induced QED radiation on equal footing with QCD. The cross section factorizes into hard parts (kept at NLO) convolved with universal lepton distribution functions (LDFs), PDFs (JAM20/CT18) and FFs (JAM20/MAP1.0), with DGLAP kernels carrying mixed QCD+QED splitting functions. Because a photon can split to qq̅ nonperturbatively, LDFs are genuinely nonperturbative objects; the authors start evolution at μ_0=m_c (not m_e) and build a “default” LDF set from a Beta-function ansatz constrained by number and momentum sum rules, then evolve to LHAPDF6-compatible grids. Headline numbers: collision-induced QED radiation reshapes the hadron p_T spectrum by up to ~50% (depleting high-p_T, enhancing low-p_T); jet spectra drop ~10–20%; scale uncertainty runs ~20–25%, but the LDF (μ_e) piece is only a few percent. Nuclear modification factors show EMC suppression below p_T∼10 GeV and Fermi-motion enhancement above.

Why it matters: this is the LDF program’s most concrete deliverable — a unified treatment of leptoproduction and photoproduction with no ad hoc Q² cut or “resolved photon” structure, exactly the framework the digest flags as sub-percent-precision machinery aimed at JLab and the EIC. The key caveat is honest and stated repeatedly: the LDFs are still model defaults (quark/gluon content set to zero at input, so those are lower limits), and existing data carry traditional radiative corrections and cannot be used to fit true LDFs until reanalyzed à la ZEUS. Dominant theory uncertainty is currently the FF choice, not the scales.

arXiv:2607.07800 — Search for axion-like particles decaying to two photons at Belle II (Belle II Collaboration et al.)

Using 408 fb⁻¹ of Belle II data, a search for e⁺e⁻→γa, a→γγ reconstructs the ALP as a narrow diphoton peak over 0.17<m_a<9.80 GeV/c², assuming photon-dominant coupling (ℬ(a→γγ)=1). Three-photon events are selected with a helicity-angle cut (|cosλ|<0.74) to suppress the dominant γγ(γ) background, a kinematic fit sharpening the mass resolution to 10–16 MeV/c², and a 19-feature neural-network classifier. No significant excess: the largest local significance is 3.3σ near m_a=0.22 GeV/c², reducing to 1.4σ global after look-elsewhere. The resulting 95% CL limits on g_aγγ reach ∼10⁻⁴ GeV⁻¹ and are the most restrictive to date over nearly all of 0.17<m_a<5.00 GeV/c² (except near 0.22 GeV/c²), improving on the prior Belle II result by up to a factor 9.

Why it matters: this cleanly extends the dark-sector portal coverage flagged in today’s digest, closing an intermediate-mass gap between beam-dump/forward limits and heavy-ion light-by-light constraints with a single tabletop-clean channel. Improvements over the 2020 Belle II analysis come from the kinematic fit, the NN, and the larger sample. Caveats are modest and disclosed: the coupling extraction ignores possible energy dependence of α_QED and g_aγγ, and η/ω mass windows are vetoed for peaking backgrounds. The mild 0.22 GeV/c² bump is statistically unremarkable.

arXiv:2607.07969 — Experimental access to the gluonic origin of the proton mass (Zein-Eddine Meziani et al.)

A concrete reconstruction scheme for the scalar gluonic trace form factor G_N(t) — the dominant, trace-anomaly source of the proton mass — from three measurable inputs. Their central identity (Eq. 14) writes G_N(t)=G_s,g(t)+G_s,q(t)-σ(t)/M: the quark scalar gravitational form factor from DVCS, the gluon scalar GFF from near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction (extracted via holographic QCD from JLab data), and the nucleon sigma-term form factor. At zero momentum transfer this reduces to G_N(0)=1-σ(0)/M_N. Plugging in the phenomenological A_q(0)=0.576±0.011 and lattice dipole/tripole GFF fits, the reconstructed G_N(t) falls rapidly with -t and agrees, within bands, with an independent lattice-QCD trace-anomaly determination — and, for -t≲1 GeV², with the interacting instanton liquid model, supporting a picture where the long-distance scalar gluonic structure is dominated by semiclassical topological glue.

Why it matters: this converts an abstract mass-decomposition question into a defined experimental program, tying together DVCS, near-threshold quarkonium, and σ-term measurements — exactly the gravitational-form-factor thread the digest has tracked this week. The lattice consistency is a genuine cross-check rather than an input. Caveats: the result relies on holographic-QCD modeling to extract G_s,g from J/ψ data and on lattice/phenomenological fits for the quark piece, so it is a proof-of-principle reconstruction rather than a fully data-driven extraction; ILM–lattice agreement degrades above -t≃1 GeV² where short-distance gluon dynamics enter.

item.title: Tuesday, July 7, 2026
item.description:
The vibe today

A neutrino-heavy day with a strong precision-theory undertow. If there was a single conversation dominating the boards, it was the one the memory has been tracking all week: as JUNO, DUNE, and Hyper-Kamiokande approach reality, the community is increasingly anxious about what could mimic a genuine CP-violating signal. Today that worry arrived in triplicate — non-unitarity, Lorentz-invariance violation, and quasi-Dirac splittings each get their own long-baseline study, and each concludes, in its own way, that the standard three-flavor picture is fragile in exactly the places DUNE hopes to measure. This is no longer a boutique concern; it reads like a coordinated stress test of the entire CP-discovery program.

The other half of the day belongs to the ongoing project of tending QCD’s foundations — hadron spectroscopy, molecular states, femtoscopic correlation functions, and the machinery of precision predictions. Here the mood is one of consolidation rather than surprise: a comprehensive instanton-vacuum framework, resonance-aware QCD+EW matching, a new fast library for gluon-initiated processes, and a fresh attempt to wrestle the muon g-2 hadronic contribution out of mutually incompatible e⁺e⁻ datasets. And, quietly notable, ATLAS lands the second GN2 calibration paper of the week — the transformer wave keeps rolling.

Underneath both currents, the day carried an unusual amount of reflection about the field itself: a global data-preservation report, a multi-agent framework for auditing AI-generated analysis code, and a historical essay on the birth of particle cosmology. A thoughtful, infrastructure-minded day rather than a bombshell one.

Themes

Neutrino oscillation degeneracies & fake CP

The week’s “fake CP” thread crests today. Singh et al. (arXiv:2607.06108) — already flagged in the memory as a benchmark — show that PMNS non-unitarity can generate sizeable CP asymmetries even at CP-conserving δ_CP, exceeding the genuine signal (~130%) in specific energy windows near 1.5 GeV, and demonstrate that a joint DUNE + Hyper-K analysis shrinks the degenerate (δ_CP,φ_21) space by up to 16×. Deka et al. (arXiv:2607.06513) run the parallel exercise for Standard-Model-Extension LIV coefficients, finding that a_ee, a_ττ, a_eμ, a_eτ can drag DUNE’s CP discovery below 3σ over a large fraction of δ_CP. And Boudjema et al. (arXiv:2607.06862) add the quasi-Dirac scenario — nearly degenerate sterile pairs from small lepton-number violation — constrained now with NOvA and T2K and forecast for DUNE. Three different new-physics dials, one shared conclusion: the CP measurement is only as clean as your assumptions about what else is in the Hamiltonian. This is the direct continuation of last week’s degeneracy-breaking theme, and the answer keeps being “combine detectors.”

Molecular states & femtoscopic correlations

A dense hadron-physics cluster, with correlation functions emerging as the tool of choice. Song et al. predict a narrow KX(3872) resonance ~50 MeV below threshold and compute its correlation function as a molecular-nature test (arXiv:2607.06317); Torres-Rincon et al. confront ALICE K^±d femtoscopy with unitarized chiral EFT plus Faddeev multiple scattering (arXiv:2607.06715). Cai et al. compute X(3872)→D̅ Dγ radiative widths in the DD̅^* molecular picture (arXiv:2607.06046). Ji et al. offer a unified NN̅ final-state-interaction reading of the near-threshold structures in e⁺e⁻ annihilation, dispensing with per-channel resonances (arXiv:2607.06168), while Ren et al. dynamically generate the Σ(1430) (but not the Σ(1385)) in isospin-violating J/ψ→Λ̅Λπ⁰ (arXiv:2607.06255). On the experimental side, BESIII reports first observation of J/ψ,ψ(3686)→pp̅ K⁰_S K⁰_S, with the branching-ratio double flavoring theory by 4.6σ (arXiv:2607.06070).

Precision QCD+EW machinery for HL-LHC

The “sub-percent precision demands joint frameworks” storyline from last week gets concrete tooling. Flower et al. present the first automated MC@NLO matching of NLO QCD+EW to an interleaved QCD+QED shower, with a resonance-aware modification for Drell-Yan (arXiv:2607.06059) — squarely in the lineage of the Lepton-Distribution-Function push the memory noted. Stremmer’s ggxy library delivers fast NLO QCD with full top-mass dependence for gg→HH, and newly gg→ZH, ZZ (arXiv:2607.06099). Coro et al. tie compact syzygy solutions for IBP reduction to Landau singularities, applied to a two-loop pentabox for pp→tt̅H (arXiv:2607.06365). And Bryzgalov et al. tackle the muon g-2 head-on, inflating uncertainties to accommodate incompatible e⁺e⁻ inputs and landing at a_μ^SM just 2σ below experiment (arXiv:2607.06352) — a reminder that the data-driven HVP is still a moving target.

Axions doing double duty

Two papers push single axions to carry multiple cosmological burdens. Delaunay et al. build a technically natural apparent-phantom dark energy from a ℤ_N-axion coupled to N dark-QCD copies, simultaneously setting the DM relic abundance and reproducing DESI’s evolving-w preference (arXiv:2607.06774). Unwin shows an intermediate-scale R-axion can evade the DFK Planckian-f_R bound via a mixed uplift and, if the R-symmetry carries a QCD anomaly, double as the QCD axion with f_R∼10¹¹ GeV yielding the observed DM (arXiv:2607.06375). Both echo last week’s habit of leaning on discrete symmetries to solve several problems at once.

Reconstruction & calibration infrastructure

ATLAS’s second GN2 calibration in a week measures b- and c-jet efficiencies simultaneously in semileptonic tt̅, reaching better than 2% (b) and 5% (c) precision (arXiv:2607.06199) — complementing the dileptonic calibration the memory highlighted. CMS reports ~96% efficiency for its upgraded GE1/1 triple-GEM endcap muon chambers, pileup-independent (arXiv:2607.06353). And Liu et al. unify α/proton/electron quenching in liquid scintillator under a single Birks coefficient by tracking sub-4-keV δ-electrons in Geant4 (arXiv:2607.05875) — a tidy fix for JUNO/SNO+ energy response.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.06108 — Quantifies exactly when fake CP from non-unitarity dominates the genuine signal, and shows the DUNE+Hyper-K combination as the cure. The reference point for the week’s degeneracy debate.
  • arXiv:2607.06862 — Quasi-Dirac oscillations constrained with real NOvA/T2K data and forecast for DUNE; a clean addition to the “what else mimics CP” catalogue.
  • arXiv:2607.06059 — First automated resonance-aware NLO QCD+EW MC@NLO matching; likely to become standard Drell-Yan precision machinery.
  • arXiv:2607.06352 — A data-driven muon g-2 that lands only 2σ from experiment by honestly inflating uncertainties over incompatible e⁺e⁻ inputs — a useful barometer for where HVP stands.
  • arXiv:2607.06060 — An ambitious dissertation building parton structure from the instanton-liquid QCD vacuum; a coherent, single-source picture bridging vacuum physics and partonic phenomenology.

From the community

Three field-facing pieces today. The DPHEP Global Report 2026 documents genuine progress in HEP data preservation — successful reanalysis of archived data, growing FAIR/open-data adoption, and a clear shift toward AI-assisted curation — while flagging long-term funding as the persistent risk (arXiv:2607.06775). Complementing it, Hammad et al. propose a multi-agent “quantity-grounded semantic differencing” framework for auditing LLM-generated collider analyses, so that AI-produced results stay reproducible and their assumptions legible (arXiv:2607.05762) — a timely governance question as such tools proliferate. And Kolb offers a historical reflection on the emergence of particle cosmology in 1980–2000 (arXiv:2607.06811).

Also noted

  • Biermann et al. argue Polyakov-loop contributions systematically soften electroweak phase transitions, disfavoring first-order PTs and weakening GW-spectrum forecasts (arXiv:2607.06203).
  • A high-precision low-Q² proton g_1 extraction from Jefferson Lab E08-027, with linked longitudinal+transverse moments for χPT comparison (arXiv:2607.05741).
  • Positivity bounds carve out a spectrahedral geometry for the dimension-eight photon–dark-photon EFT (arXiv:2607.06658).

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.06108 — Non-Unitarity Effects and Fake CP Violation in Neutrino Oscillation Experiments (Pratima Singh et al.)

Using GLoBES with a custom non-unitary probability engine, Singh et al. quantify how a single off-diagonal PMNS deviation α_21=|α_21|e^iφ_21 fakes CP violation at DUNE and Hyper-K. The headline: at each experiment’s oscillation maximum the fake asymmetry is a mild perturbation (1.7% of the genuine swing at DUNE’s 2.4 GeV, 4.5% at Hyper-K’s 0.5 GeV for |α_21|=0.01), but in suppressed-genuine windows near 1.5–1.6 GeV the fake-to-genuine ratio exceeds unity — 129% at DUNE, 134% at Hyper-K, with a second 129% window for Hyper-K at 2.0 GeV. In these bins an A_CP-only analysis cannot separate real from fake CP, and the sign of φ_21 is invisible in the broad-peak region. The degeneracy analysis shows Hyper-K alone leaves φ_21 essentially unconstrained at ≥2σ (matter effects too weak to reject the wrong ordering, χ²_min=4.4), while DUNE’s 1300 km matter lever arm pins it (χ²_min=486). Their combination shrinks the 3σ allowed (δ_CP,φ_21) area to 0.059π² — 16.3× smaller than Hyper-K alone.

Why it matters: this is the week’s reference point for “fake CP.” It concretely localizes where non-unitarity is dangerous (specific energy bins, not the oscillation maximum) and confirms the recurring prescription — combine complementary baselines rather than trusting either detector. Caveat: only the minimal single-parameter α_21=0.01 scenario is explored, and the combined 3σ area is marginally larger than DUNE alone, an honestly-flagged artifact of Hyper-K’s flat directions overlapping DUNE’s contour edge.

arXiv:2607.06862 — Probing Quasi-Dirac Neutrino Oscillations at Long Baseline Experiments (Noor-Ines Boudjema et al.)

Boudjema, Deppisch & Pattanaik embed the quasi-Dirac scenario — small lepton-number-violating Majorana mass μ splitting a near-degenerate sterile pair — in an inverse-seesaw-motivated 3+2 framework, deriving analytic ν_μ→ν_e and ν_μ→ν_μ probabilities with the sterile splitting Δm²_54∝μ driving a slow interference term. Simulating NOvA, T2K and DUNE in GLoBES with full systematics, they map sensitivity in (θ_sa,Δm²_54). Current NOvA and T2K each reach θ_sa≈0.1; combined, ≈0.08. DUNE alone dominates, probing θ_sa≈0.05 — roughly a factor-two improvement — with approximately uniform coverage across Δm²_54 because its long baseline averages out the rapid sterile oscillations. NOvA/T2K instead show a resonance enhancement near Δm²_54∼Δm²_31∼2.4×10⁻³ eV², plus degeneracy valleys at θ_sa≈θ_23≈0.4 where the 5ν model mimics 3ν.

Why it matters: this adds quasi-Dirac splittings to the week’s “what mimics CP” catalogue, now constrained with real NOvA/T2K data rather than forecasts alone. A key structural result is that quasi-Dirac sensitivity is intrinsically coupled to δ_CP: the 5ν appearance probability carries a c_sa suppression factor modulating the CP-dependent amplitude, so DUNE’s quasi-Dirac and CP programs necessarily inform one another. Caveats: flavour-universal sterile mixing (θ_sa common to all angles) and vanishing sterile CP phases are assumed throughout — both acknowledged as simplifications that could resolve or deepen the identified degeneracies. Current NOvA/T2K cannot exclude the scenario across benchmark phases and orderings.

arXiv:2607.06059 — A resonance-aware MC@NLO QCD+EW-matched calculation of lepton-pair production (Lois Flower et al.)

Flower, Roper & Schönherr present the first automated MC@NLO matching of NLO QCD+EW to an interleaved QCD+QED parton shower, built on Catani-Seymour dipoles in SHERPA. The core technical contribution is a resonance-aware modification: dipoles spanning a colour/charge-neutral s-channel resonance are switched off (via Θ-functions on emission scale t_res∼Γ_r² and virtuality measure Δ_r) when an emission is hard enough to resolve it, preventing spurious recoil-induced distortions of the resonance lineshape. They also identify that standard interleaved matching leaves uncancelled 𝒪(α_sα) terms — the QCD Sudakov Δ̅≪1 multiplying QED dipoles drives the photon p_⊥ spectrum negative over 15–40 GeV — and cure it with an extra physically-motivated Sudakov on the H-events (dubbed MC@NLO^sud), at the cost of a formally higher-order shift to the inclusive cross section.

Validated against fixed-order NLO QCD+EW and against MC@NLO QCD+YFS, the method gives, for pp→e⁺e⁻, a resonance-aware distortion of the dressed dilepton mass of a few per mille (0.2% below the Z peak, 0.5% at m_ee≈60 GeV) and a percent-level change in hard-photon p_⊥, rising to +15% at p_⊥,γ≈1 TeV from missing ISR-FSR interference. Why it matters: Drell-Yan underpins calibration, PDF extraction and normalization, so this is likely to become standard HL-LHC precision machinery. Caveat: the resonance-aware implementation is currently process-specific (though the algorithm is general), and colour/charged resonances need new emitter/spectator splitting functions left to future work.

item.title: Monday, July 6, 2026
item.description:
The vibe today

A broad, foundational sort of day — the kind where no single bombshell dominates but several sturdy pillars go up at once. Two results that the week’s memory already flags as turning points actually land here: CMS’s first direct assault on the triple-Higgs coupling space (arXiv:2607.05145) and ATLAS’s calibration of the transformer-based GN2 tagger on Run 3 data (arXiv:2607.05322). Both feel less like surprises than like the field methodically converting years of instrumentation and theory into hard numbers on the coupling landscape.

Underneath the LHC headlines, the mood is unmistakably QCD-flavored. A cluster of papers reaches into the nonperturbative interior of hadrons — pion distribution amplitudes, proton gravitational form factors, the analytic structure of the effective charge and its link to confinement — while dense-matter QCD shows up through lattice two-color simulations and anomalous Wess-Zumino-Witten terms. This is not new physics; it is the field tending its foundations, and doing so with real ambition.

The other half of the room is chasing dark matter, and the tone there is one of pressure and pivoting. Under the shadow of LZ limits, higgsino WIMPs get their blind-spot escape routes closed off, while others turn to vector dark matter, self-interacting halos, cosmic-ray-DM collisions, and laboratory photon experiments. It’s a scattered, exploratory energy — the sound of a community probing every remaining seam.

Themes

Nonperturbative QCD and the guts of hadrons

Today’s densest thread. Lei Chang and collaborators deliver the first functional-QCD calculation of the pion distribution amplitude via LaMET within the fRG (arXiv:2607.04871), reporting a second moment notably smaller than lattice-LaMET determinations — a tension worth watching. Kim et al. present the flavor-decomposed gravitational form factors and mechanical structure of the proton, isolating the twist-4 c̅ term and finding a sizable strange-quark contribution to the D-term (arXiv:2607.05079). Deur offers an unusually intuitive picture, tracing confinement to two conjugate singularities in the effective charge α_g_1 and reading off exponentially suppressed parton propagators at long distance (arXiv:2607.05144). Rounding it out: two-color lattice QCD finding a superfluid sound speed above the conformal bound (arXiv:2607.04624), and WZW terms for neutral mesons under magnetic field and rotation (arXiv:2607.04929). Collectively, a strong statement that hadron structure and dense-matter QCD remain fertile, first-principles ground.

Dark sector under pressure — and pivoting

Baer et al. ask whether direct-detection blind spots can save light higgsino dark matter and answer, bluntly, no: the surviving cancellations all sit in the unnatural regime, pushing natural SUSY toward unstable higgsinos (arXiv:2607.05648) — a direct continuation of the LZ-cornered-WIMP storyline the memory has been tracking. Elsewhere the response is to look somewhere new: Higgsed vector dark matter via parametric resonance, reframed as a probe of inflationary initial conditions (arXiv:2607.05309); a fresh Monte-Carlo SIDM implementation in AREPO-2 for gravothermal core collapse (arXiv:2607.05504); keV-scale DM limits from Galactic cosmic-ray–DM scattering seen in ANTARES neutrinos (arXiv:2607.05335); and two laboratory photon-based searches — an X-ray light-shining-through-walls proposal at HEPS for dark photons (arXiv:2607.05288) and a Breit-Wheeler pair-production channel for MeV-scale ALPs with a Fano-type interference signature (arXiv:2607.05572). The WIMP is cornered; the search is diversifying.

The Higgs self-coupling, made experimental

CMS’s nonresonant HHH→6b search sets the most stringent limit yet on triple-Higgs production and, crucially, excludes for the first time a slice of (κ_3,κ_4) space previously bounded only by perturbative unitarity (arXiv:2607.05145). Complementing the scalar-sector push from below, Ashanujjaman et al. reinterpret ATLAS tt̅ bb̅ measurements to constrain a light charged Higgs through the near-threshold H^±→t^*b channel (arXiv:2607.05499) — a genuinely underexplored window, and yet another EFT-style reinterpretation of existing fiducial data, echoing a habit the memory has noted becoming standard.

Reconstruction infrastructure keeps maturing

The GN2 flavor-tagger calibration in dileptonic tt̅ (arXiv:2607.05322) reports up to 2–3× better light/charm rejection over DL1d, with ~1% uncertainty at high p_T — the transformer wave the memory has been following, now benchmarked. On the tracking side, a hybrid Hough-transform-plus-CNN scheme suppresses spurious HL-LHC track candidates by learning directly on the parameter-space image (arXiv:2607.04723). Detector hardware fills in around it: WLS fibers for VUV scintillation in high-pressure noble TPCs (arXiv:2607.04944), MOSFET diagnostics for p-stop isolation in silicon sensors (arXiv:2607.05528), and the fully-digital PUEO beamformer trigger (arXiv:2607.05285).

Neutrinos and light-element inputs

The precision-inputs mindset extends to neutrinos. Ishidoshiro pushes 0νββ beyond half-life limits toward stability of the operator-level interpretation across isotopes and NME methods, finding light-Majorana exchange the most robust (arXiv:2607.04932). Long et al.’s relic-neutrino-wind exposure penalty (arXiv:2607.05221) — a sobering 10⁵ factor — also appears here. And in a methodological standout, Tait recasts d(p,γ)³He capture as an on-shell-amplitude EFT, tracing the LUNA–vs–ab initio offset in BBN to a single natural next-to-leading contact term (arXiv:2607.05514).

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.05145 — CMS puts experimental teeth into (κ_3,κ_4) for the first time; the quartic-coupling frontier is now data-driven.
  • arXiv:2607.05322 — GN2 calibrated on Run 3: the transformer tagger is now a production tool, not a demo.
  • arXiv:2607.05514 — On-shell amplitude methods applied to low-energy nuclear capture; a clean template that could ripple through BBN reaction networks.
  • arXiv:2607.05144 — A physically transparent reading of confinement from the analytic structure of an observable coupling.
  • arXiv:2607.05517 — Global monopole networks are shown not to follow constant scaling, undercutting a common assumption in defect-DM and GW forecasts.

From the community

One field-culture paper: a benchmarking study of the energy footprint of Monte Carlo event generators, arguing that thoughtful multithreading can meaningfully cut the “watts per event” as HEP looks beyond the LHC era (arXiv:2607.05018). Computing sustainability continues its slow move from afterthought to design criterion.

Also noted

  • BESIII observes χ_cJ→pK⁻Λ̅η for the first time, with Λ(1520) and Λ̅(1690) structures (arXiv:2607.05041).
  • Predicted antibottom-strange molecular pentaquarks near BΣ/B^*Σ thresholds, 6.44–6.52 GeV (arXiv:2607.04679).
  • Smooth sign-switching dark energy stays compatible with full CMB+DESI+Pantheon+ while easing H_0 tension (arXiv:2607.05044).

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.05145 — Search for nonresonant triple Higgs boson production in the six-b-quark final state at √s = 13 TeV (CMS Collaboration)

Using the full Run 2 dataset (138 fb⁻¹), CMS performs the first nonresonant HHH→6b search built around an inclusive transformer/SPANet reconstruction that spans all resolved-to-merged topologies (three H from small-radius jet pairs, from large-radius jets, or mixtures). A two-stage SPANet classifier plus a data-driven QCD-multijet model (95% of background) with b/bb-tag score resampling yields no excess. The observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit is 44 (43) fb, or 588 (572)× the SM σ^HHH_ggF=0.08 fb — the most stringent triple-Higgs bound to date. In the coupling framework, -7.4<κ_3<12.4 (for κ_4=1) and -177<κ_4<185 (for κ_3=1), improving on ATLAS’s earlier 6b result (-11<κ_3<17; -230<κ_4<240).

Why it matters: the two-parameter (κ_3,κ_4) scan, for the first time in a direct HHH search, excludes a slice of parameter space previously bounded only by perturbative unitarity — pushing the quartic-coupling frontier from theory into data, as the digest flags. Sensitivity is limited by data statistics (~52% of the expected limit), with the QCD-multijet shape the leading systematic. Honest caveats: the coupling scans assume SM signal topology at every coupling value (cross-section-only scaling), and κ_4-dependent kinematic/shape effects in HH are deferred; including realistic kinematics degrades the expected κ_3 bound by 12–15%. The HH contribution is fixed to μ_HH=1 with profiled uncertainty. HL-LHC projections (S3 scenario) are provided but the current constraint remains ~600× SM.

arXiv:2607.05322 — b-jet identification efficiency for GN2 in dileptonic tt̄ at √s = 13.6 TeV (The ATLAS Collaboration)

(Abstract only.) ATLAS calibrates the transformer-based GN2 flavour tagger on 56 fb⁻¹ of 2022–2023 Run 3 data, extracting the b-jet efficiency and jet-flavour composition simultaneously from a tt̅-enriched dileptonic sample, binned in jet p_T (20–400 GeV) across six cumulative-efficiency working points. GN2 delivers up to 2× (3×) higher light-flavour (charm) rejection than its predecessor DL1d at fixed b-efficiency. Data/simulation correction factors fall in 0.9–1.3, with total uncertainty around 1% for p_T>60 GeV in the loosest ([65%,0%]) interval.

Why it matters: this converts GN2 from demonstrator to calibrated production tool on Run 3 data, backing the digest’s “transformer wave” theme with benchmarked numbers — the same tagging performance that underpins searches like the HHH→6b analysis above. The ~1% high-p_T uncertainty sets the achievable precision for the many Run 3 analyses that will now adopt GN2.

arXiv:2607.05514 — Deuterium-Proton Fusion in an EFT Constructed from On-Shell Amplitudes (Tim M. P. Tait)

Tait builds d(p,γ)³He radiative capture as a nuclear-state EFT in which deuteron, proton, and ³He are point-like degrees of freedom, and constructs the amplitude entirely from on-shell methods — massive spinor-helicity three-point vertices, BCFW recursion, and an enumerated tower of transverse boundary (two-body-current) operators — bypassing any Lagrangian. The expansion parameter is p_rel/p_* with p_≈53 MeV set by deuteron breakup, giving a contact-operator scale Λ=√(4π) p_≈187 MeV. A global Bayesian fit to LUNA/Türkat capture data plus ³He ANC and NDA priors returns S(0)=0.209±0.008 eV b (between Solar Fusion III’s 0.203 and Marcucci’s ab initio 0.216), with χ²/dof=0.83.

The headline physics result: the persistent offset between the ab initio benchmark and the sub-percent LUNA data is traced to a single natural-sized next-to-leading E1 contact term, t_E1≃-0.146±0.021 (~15% amplitude, ~30% rate deficit), degenerate with a ~15%-lower effective ³He asymptotic normalization. This recasts the PRIMAT–PArthENoPE split (a ~2σ D/H discrepancy) from a choice between curves into a measurable low-energy constant. Caveats stated plainly: the angle-integrated S-factor cannot separate the contact term from the ANC (a precise p–d doublet elastic measurement is proposed), Türkat data sit ~2.3σ high and are floated, quadrupole contacts are prior-limited, and the analytic work was AI-assisted (Claude), human-validated.

item.title: Sunday, July 5, 2026
item.description:
The vibe today

Today’s digest highlights a community deeply invested in the “co-design” paradigm: the idea that our hardware (detectors, triggers) and our theory (SMEFT operators, GPD extraction) can no longer be optimized in isolation. We are seeing a concerted push to embed heavy computational machinery—like GPU-accelerated Hough transforms or neural-network-optimized trigger templates—directly into the infrastructure of proposed high-luminosity facilities like the STCF.

The theoretical mood is equally rigorous. The field is moving beyond broad-brush searches for new physics toward a granular, “precision-first” approach. Whether it’s the refined mapping of gluon GPDs for the EIC, or the emergence of “protected” composite Higgs states defined by lattice-verified collective kernels, the emphasis is on identifying observables that are resilient to the noise of standard model backgrounds. It is a day characterized by meticulous technical progress, where the tools of the trade—from lattice QCD to real-time pattern matching—are being sharpened for an era where the signals we seek are buried deeper than ever.

Themes

STCF Infrastructure and Reconstruction

The proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF) is clearly serving as a testing ground for the next generation of online data processing. As high-luminosity electron-positron environments push occupancy and data-throughput limits, the field is abandoning CPU-bound traditional reconstruction in favor of GPU-centric paradigms. Peng et al. arXiv:2607.04067 and Guo et al. arXiv:2607.04271 present a sophisticated co-design framework for the STCF Main Drift Chamber (MDC). By leveraging GPU-accelerated matrix-based Hough transforms and neural-network-assisted template libraries, they achieve significant speedups (over 150x for track reconstruction) without compromising signal retention. This work signals a broader cultural shift toward deterministic, high-speed, parallelizable trigger algorithms that do not sacrifice physics accuracy.

SMEFT and Higgs-Sector Modernization

The EFT-reinterpretation of LHC data remains a primary language for weak-scale searches, but it is becoming increasingly sophisticated. Gillies et al. arXiv:2607.04251 illustrate the necessity of including dimension-8 operators to maintain the validity of Effective Field Theory (EFT) predictions in boosted W⁺W⁻ production, noting that the γγ →WW channel offers a unique, cleaner window into these effects. Meanwhile, on the composite Higgs front, Abbas arXiv:2607.04136 offers a compelling theoretical mechanism—the “protected collective eigenmode”—that moves beyond standard “accidental” fine-tuning, providing a concrete, lattice-testable path to a light Higgs in strong-coupling scenarios.

Axion-Portal Diversification

The axion remains a primary focus, but the search strategies are branching out into novel topologies. Long et al. arXiv:2607.04128 explore the DFSZ model’s potential through the lens of scalar coupling modifiers, while Guo et al. arXiv:2607.04137 propose a MeV-scale dark QCD sector to address the axion domain wall problem. Complementing these theoretical developments, Chen et al. arXiv:2607.04155 propose a high-sensitivity Penning trap experiment to push axion-photon coupling limits using photon regeneration, and Matsuoka et al. arXiv:2607.04550 leverage binary polarimetry as a novel astrophysical probe for axion-induced birefringence.

Precision QCD and GPD Mapping

As we build toward the EIC, the community is refining the ways we probe proton structure. Pang et al. arXiv:2607.04482 demonstrate that exclusive dijet production—both quark and gluon—serves as an essential probe of Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs). This is paired with the work of the MMGPDs Collaboration arXiv:2607.04481, who use exclusive photon leptoproduction data to reconcile tensions in the proton charge-radius puzzle. Together, these papers highlight the move toward multi-channel analyses that integrate varied data sets to construct a self-consistent picture of proton structure at high energies.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.04067 GPU-Accelerated Matrix-Based Hough Transform for Online Track Reconstruction in the STCF MDC — Peng et al. (hep-ex)
  • arXiv:2607.04271 Neural-Network-Assisted Binary Template Construction for Matrix-Based Pattern Matching in the STCF MDC — Guo et al. (hep-ex)
  • arXiv:2607.04136 Naturally Light Composite Higgs as a Protected Collective Eigenmode — Abbas (hep-ph)
  • arXiv:2607.04251 Anomalous triple gauge couplings in the light of dimension-8 operators in W⁺W⁻ — Gillies et al. (hep-ph)
